author: Ravenstone
subject: Arms Warrior - Increased Weapon Skill Talent
content_md:
I'm aware that there have been several +weapon skill increasing items made available to us, including some specifically for 2h weapons, which are great and a step in the right direction to giving more balance to weapon skills. Loving them. However, I feel like some specs should get additional help in the talent trees. Arms Warrior being one of them.

I'd like to propose weapon skill be provided to all 2H Weapons via the Two-Handed Weapon Specialization talent. I'd suggest 2 per talent to a max of 10 since I feel it wouldn't make too much of a difference build wise.

Weapon Skill doesn't affect BG PvP [at all](https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_skill) (see Player attacking a Player section) so this doesn't buff the standard PvP Arms Warrior, and since it'd be limited to 2H weapons won't affect DW Fury DPS either. 2H Fury is the only real beneficiary of this proposal, which could use a little help.

Thematically, I've always thought it was incredibly odd that Warrior Arms spec didn't include any way to increase Weapon Skill much like Rogue's Weapon Expertise talent. I always imagined Arms as a master of their weapons, having trained extensively and as such having those specific Weapon Specialisations. I also thought this change could potentially be extended to Enh Shamans and Ret Paladins, as they both have real PvE damage concerns, but I feel there is more of a case for Warriors to get this.

Anyway, let me know what you think, or if I've missed a glaringly obvious problem here.

This is the impact of Weapon Skill for melee strikes.

Weapon skill is specifically advantageous and desirable for dual wield melee. While +8 weapon skill on items such as Obsidian Edged Blade are a boon, 5 talent points for 10 skill would not likely be super attractive (against the value in Fury), nor improve the PvE preference for Arms Warriors.

 10 skill will save the 2H warrior the need for 3% gear hit, and a modest portion of their damage (white glancing blows) will improve by 30%.

If you want to improve the Arms warrior's lot in raid, it may be best to allow their utility (reducing healing by 50%, stronger AOE potential) to shine in the raid and dungeon environment. Warriors, as you have probably heard, have few issues in vanilla. They do have some, and they are worthy to improve upon:
- Odd order of talents in the Prot Tree
- Unimaginative utility in Arms
- Lacking a "Bleed Build" featuring Rend
Some people would also rather Arms simply be a PVP spec.

Wouldnt directly say Weapon Skill is somehow going to make 2H warriors 'better' because there are already +7skill items for basically everything (tho mace is Horde only RIP), and 7 is just a mere ~2% shy of highest diminishing returns.

The issue is just a mix of itemization (youre forever stuck in gloves or one of two helms) and the hanging-on meta scene that thinks if youre not wearing giga-BiS and parsing 99% that you're guilty of inferiority thus warriors are too spooked by the idea of wearing one item for the rest of eternity (all the while telling the cat to go farm a lvl 30 blue-hander for their entire life).

 2H war is basically just semi-meh because they dont build rage as fast to spam like DW Fury does, and debuff limit locking them out of 100% Deep Wounds uptime/MS. They're practically similar to every other melee that isnt warrior because of it: you just dont mash buttons on GCD like a coked-out labrat thus you dont put out the damage by comparison.

Ferals are in much worse need of some attack skill than anybody else since theyre permanently stuck at 300, and we're still at a point that DW Fury could likely just receive actual nerfs rather than widesweep buffs to all other classes to start.

author: Iambuck
subject: Re: Is warrior tanking difficult?
content_md:
In dungeons as a tank you'll be the success or failing factor. If you know how to manage to following points you have no reason to fail :
 - hold effective aggro
 - know the dungeons (the difficult packs, the patrols, the boss mechanics)
 - put up marks on mobs for your dps to focus
 - call out dps/heals when they do something wrong, you should be the group leader as a tank

In other words you need to chew-up the work for everyone.

Then for raids you take the same points but to a bigger extent. Also if you plan on being the main tank, i advise you pick an off-tank you know AND you trust. Every raid needs an off tank and the off tank role can be very specific fight per fight. I would say sometimes harder as offtank as you need to be more reactive than pro-active

subject: Re: Is warrior tanking difficult?
content_md:
Without doubt, tank is one of the more challenging roles in dungeons, especially for trash groups, but a lot depends on how the group cooperates.

Many dps players think they're already doing a good job if they only gear up nicely and make big numbers, but that's far from true.

Good dps will watch their own aggro, avoid cleave and AE damage, focus targets (either as marked by the tank or just based on the given situation, like killing healers and casters first), help out with CC (at least when asked to do so), peel the occasional mob off your healer, finish of runners, kite aggroed mobs to you instead of letting you run all over the place and then do nice numbers as icing on the cake. If people do all these things, tanking and healing becomes much easier.

An experienced tank can compensate a lack of good gameplay from others to some extent, but you shouldn't be afraid to tell people (politely!) to adjust their game so that you can safely tank your way through a dungeon.

Of course, a tank needs to learn their class, too, but often, when difficulty ramps up, it's because of inexperienced or entitled group members and a lack of teamwork.

author: Guilliman
subject: Warrior spell change for shield wall, recklesness and retaliation
content_md:
Hello,

Would it be great if for the next patch warriors get a nerf for their three 30min CD spells retaliation, Recklesness and shield wall, but with the added benefit of shortening their CD time. Thus making them more usable in fights and not saving them all the time, which basically prevents you from using them.

The change was originally made in wotlk and I will quote the text from a changelog for wotlk from some gaming website from 2009:

"If you've been playing a warrior for a long time, you've probably gotten used to the way your three big class abilities work. Presently, Shield Wall, Retaliation and Recklessness are linked abilities with a shared 30 minute cooldown. This means if you use one of them you can't use any of the other two in addition to the one you used for half an hour. Not only has this restriction kept warriors from using any of their big cooldowns in Arenas, it also serves as an inhibitor in raiding and soloing and questing. You don't pop Shield Wall unless you're absolutely sure you're going to die, because then you won't have it for possibly two or three boss attempts.

This will no longer be the case in Wrath. In a move that simultaneously nerfs and buffs these long-standing warrior abilities, the base effect of each has been reduced but their cooldown shortened to 5 minutes. The tooltips of each ability spell it out now. The duration of each has dropped to about 12 seconds (not a huge deal), Recklessness has lost its fear breaking ability, Shield Wall only reduces incoming damage by 50%, and Retaliation only hits 20 attacks now. Yes, these are all nerfs. But the upside of a 5 minute duration makes them far more friendly for use. You can pop shield wall on trash if needed and still have it for a boss. A fury warrior can use reck secure in the knowledge that he'll most likely have it back up by the time the boss hits execute range. And retaliation might even be viable for multi-mob tanking now! A little stance dancing and you don't have to fret that shield wall is gone for half an hour.

To me, this is an awesome change. It makes those abilities less restricted and thus, makes me more willing to use them."

End of quote.

Whadda you think peeps?

Edit: source: [https://www.engadget.com/2008-08-10-war ... h1dT3ojjMx](https://www.engadget.com/2008-08-10-warriors-will-be-cooling-down-faster-in-northrend.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAB1hgiXd6sG84BBI_riBGOUGPcSg2VYz9J7ydh8H6_rguMoI7cf-1R_hzdTplZM0WJkAkW1OnCqnqUIhk394YcREgdMiXvDP24IBDAMomOmZc4n_Yc8-Wd7xpoj0pRTCz_WmZFIe_ePJoFHmK9RPbogjzO9VqGm-FUh1dT3ojjMx)

And thirdly and most importantly. Classic isnt built to be "convinient". It is meant to be fun. And popping a 30+ min cd and turning into a god is fun. And id take this over some meter monkeying cd that is pressed every pull any day of the week

author: Kremmen
subject: Re: Warrior Macro
content_md:
For starters, install the addon Roid Macros. It'll make creating macros much easier.
A Shield Bash macro would go like: Code: Select all

```
#showtooltip Shield Bash
/equip [your shield name here]
/equip [your one-hander name here]
/cast Defensive Stance
/cast Shield Bash
/startattack
```

Then you can create a weapon switch macro to swap between your sword & board or your two-hander, like: Code: Select all

```
/equip [your shield name here]
/equip [your one-hander name here]
/equip [your two-hander name here]
```

This will switch you to your sword & board if you have your two-hander equipped and vice versa.
ShaguTweaks has a function that will automatically switch stances for you if you press an ability that requires you to be in particular stance to perform it, so you can remove "/cast [stance name]" from your macros. There's even a standalone version of this feature so if you don't want to use ShaguTweaks as a whole you can just use that.

author: Drunkenrobot
subject: Arms PvE Changes
content_md:
[*This post is a copy of a discord suggestion by Jaekta (Azerty#6396) in the #warrior channel.*]

Hey guys, me and my fellow warriors in <Cold Embrace> have been discussing the recent announcement about the feedback that will be asked on possible class changes.
I am a purely PvE guy so my feedback wille be exclusively focused on that with the intent to neither buff nor nerf warrior in PvP Ill let others provide feedback on the matter.

The crux of the matter:
Warriors are known as the most overpowered class in the game, best tank, best DPS , insane potential and mechanics.
I'm here to argue that this is not the case in fact it is quite the contrary. Fury is overpowered, a combination of Rage, Death Wish, Flurry and the linear scaling of Bloodthirst makes it punch way above the other two talent trees which are known as complete jokes in PvE. both Deep Prot and Deep Arms are complete and utter garbage and that's why DPS AND Tanks go 31 points into Fury.

My aim with this feedback is to make Arms and Prot, if not optimal, at least viable in PvE keep in mind that these changes follow 3 rules:
- They do not have any noticeable impact in PvP
- They cannot in any way shape or form benefit Fury and as such should be in the 5th, 6th or 7th talent row of their trees
- They are independent changes, it is not an all or nothing and work on their own.

 **Arms:**
Arms as a dps spec suffers from being a purely PvP spec that provides 0 utility in most PvE single target situation, they are meant to be the 2 Handed spec but are utterly beaten by 2 Handed fury due to the inaccessibility of Flurry and the fact that Mortal Strike scales off of weapon damage compared to the AP linear scaling of Bloodthirst.
When I heard the word "Arms warrior" what do I picture ? Well it's in the name : a Master of Arms, one who is patient, calculated and strikes with a single blow that defeats their oponent, if I were to think about what NPC is an arms warrior in Vanilla it would be Instructor Razuvius a master who teaches and can destroy anyone with one attack.

 **To better represent that here are my suggested changes:**
- **Poleaxe Specialization x/5:**
Increases your chance to get a critical strike with axes and polearms by 1%/2%/3%/4%/5% and increases Two-Handed Axes and Polearms Weapon skill by 2/4/6/8/10.
- **Mace Specialization x/5:**
Gives you a 1%/2%/3%/4%/5% chance to stun your target for 3 seconds with a Mace and increases Two-Handed Maces Weapon skill by 2/4/6/8/10.
- **Sword Specialization x/5:**
Gives you a 1%/2%/3%/4%/5% chance to get an extra attack on the same target after dealing damage with your swords and increases Two-Handed Sword Weapon skill by 2/4/6/8/10.
The point of these changes is that, as a Master of Arms it seems obvious that the Arms warrior would know how to use his weapons to the fullest of their ability, weapon skills is one of the few mechanics that does not interact with PvP. 10 might seem to be a lot but this is also a way to fix the grossly unfair advantage humans orcs and goblins get with their racials which should have been removed a long time ago. with 10 weapon skill available in a spec non-meta races have at least one spec that allows them to not be a burden just because they made a "mistake" at character creation.

- **Improved Discipline:**
Reduces the cooldown of your retaliation, recklessness and shield wall abilities by 6/12/18 min.
As a master of his emotions and a composed fighter the Arms warrior is able to always fall back on his training, he knows when to hold back, when to defend and when to go all out.
adding weapon skill to arms is one way to augment the damage of the arms warrior in PvE but it in no way makes it viable, you would still be 15%-20% weaker than a fury just due to lack of BT and Flury. The way to fix this would be to make recklessness available on pretty much every boss (or at least every two bosses) for Arms warrior which would provide a noticeable 'but not broken) boost.
Although this change might seem super impactful in PvP I believe that it doesn't really matter in the grand scheme of things : either the warrior you face has Retaliation up or not and the way to deal with him is still the same : kill their pocket healer and wait for retaliation to go down.

If the availability of retaliation is too much to handle the talent could be changed instead to :

- **Improved Discipline:**
Reduces the cooldown of your retaliation and shield wall abilities by 2/4/6 min and reduces the cooldown of your recklessness  ability by 6/12/18 min.
Those are my suggestions for Arms

content_md:
1. Arms won't do as much damage as a fury with 2h weapon, no matter how much buff you let Arms.

Therefore, the best way to update the Arms spec in PvE is to make it a support spec. Since it was done in TBC. The buff that increases PD of entire raid.

![Image](https://i.postimg.cc/Y2QrffKy/2023-06-24-014950703.png)

 2. It is unlikely that the Turtle team will change the Arms Spec for PVE. Admins really don't like warriors who haven't received any changes. Only visual or useless things.
For example poleaxe spec. A warrior cannot carry both a polearm and an ax at the same time.
He always chose one of those because it's a two-handed weapon. Although all types of weapons can be combined into one talent, you will still only equip one thing.

With this, they freed up one talent cell and put useless Improved Disciplines there, which no one takes, because it is very weak to spend talent points on it. They gave them useless -2/4/6 minutes on Improved Disciplines. Instead of -4/7/10 analogies with TBC. And the fact that no warrior takes this useless talent does not mean anything to them. Many patches have passed but they have not changed this talent. You write about some -6/12/18 it's funny.

 3. Giving a weapon skill bonus only for two-handed is a bad idea, because it will lead to an imbalance for those who want to play arms with two one-handed or one-handed and a shield. Yes, they don't play like that, but now there is such an opportunity. What you suggest also takes away this opportunity.

The problem of the warrior is not in pvE. Everything is fine there. You can play with 2h or two 1h.
Warrior problem is absolutely the weakest class in pvp. Without Second Wind and some kind of sustain, it's a piece of meat. Your topic distracts from the real problems of the warrior.

author: Gnomoerectus
subject: Re: warrior improve
content_md:
It's true that Fury does too much damage. Warrior players might not like it but I think the Warrior class fantasy is that they're hard to kill, not that they're stealthless rogues that can turn an enemy to mincemeat as long as someone else is tanking them. Nerfing fury's damage and buffing their self-heal (rework blood craze, buff bloodthirst self-heal) would be interesting.

It's also true that rend is a joke and so is the deep prot tree.
It would be nice if warrior could be rebalanced by redistributing some of the damage fury deals across the other two specs.

I would be more interested in spending points in deep prot if revenge and shield slam actually did decent damage, maybe even enough that leveling in prot spec cpupd be considered an option.

It would also be nice if stance-dancing and applying rend as fury was a dps increase because it would increase the skill cap.

author: Bigsmerf
subject: Re: Do warriors get better in endgame PVP/PVE?
content_md: Warrior (At least fury and fury/prot) warrior is the best DPS and best tank at endgame with gear. And even without it you're very solid. Arms is actually a decent spec for DPS in endgame simply due to warrior scaling as well as it does, but fury is your best bet. Now, PvP wise, you're kinda fucked. Warrior, even as arms, the best PvP spec for the class, you'll be pretty underwhelming in most situations especially without help. Sure, you can pump big numbers and hit hard, but that isn't worth much when most classes can either kite you, or other melee classes have some sort of way to counter or disable you. (Rogues usually have the opening and stunlock until you're dead. Paladin is just... Paladin... Druid can bear and frenzied regen, or kite. I'm not sure on shammy, but they can kite a bit against warrior too.)

author: Tomberry
subject: Re: When should I change from Arms to Fury
content_md:
You don't need the 9% immediately.
This is the end-value for lvl 63 (Raidbosses) and ensures that your skills don't miss. Whitehits will still miss, but that's unavoidable.

For lvl 60 dungeons ~5% are fine. No need to min-max here.

If you respecc to fury while leveling, don't fight mobs that have a higher level than you. You will miss a lot, what is a bit frustrating. But as a warrior you shouldn't do that anyway.

But the most important thing is fun. Play what you like more.

This is a build I thought up on a whim for the heck of it. I am in no way a warrior expert and my highest level one on the server is 27, so this will likely have flaws, but I'm into the idea. I'll go through the basic concept.

Unfortunately I can't put enough points into fury for flurry though, and I don't know of any ways to properly circumvent this.

author: Mativh
subject: Re: Deep Prot Ideas
content_md:
Reply:
> **Wilsonsds wrote: Mon Nov 06, 2023 11:54 pm**
> 1) Change One-Handed Weapon Specialization into Sword And Shield Specialization. That still gives 10% for one-handed weapons, but gives a bonus THREAT based on your defense skill. IF YOU ARE USING A SHIELD

There are many other talents addressing the shield-wielding capabilities of the prot war, this one is ment to address the weapon of choice, a one handed weapon, which a good prot war needs to master as well. Instead of a threat increase without apparent reason, add to the talent up to +5 one handed weapons skill which would contribute to threat generation in a more meaningful way.

> **Wilsonsds wrote: Mon Nov 06, 2023 11:54 pm**
> 2) Change Shield Slam to a 10 secs Cooldown and cost of 15 rage. And instead of debuffing a magic on the target, make the target unable to move for 5 secs.

The concept of slamming the shield so powerfully that a buff gets knocked off a target is interesting, but I think it should happen only upon a critical hit, and accompanied by a knockback on the target. I agree with the 10 sec & 15 rage change.

> **Wilsonsds wrote: Mon Nov 06, 2023 11:54 pm**
> 3) You be able to use revenge everytime with a fixed cooldown, but the proc make it instant to cast it again.

I disagree. The concept of Revenge is to respond to an enemies attempt to attack you, which you have stopped. It is an inverse Overpower, shouldn't be useable all the time. However, a Revenge should be indeed instant after a block/parry/dodge, not with a resetted cooldown, but simply useable right away instead of waiting for a cooldown while it is useable, that never made sense. (See below)

Prot tree revisioned:

Toughness compressed into 3 ranks; 3/6/10%, instead of 2/4/6/8/10%.

Iron Will compressed into 3 ranks; 5/10/15% resist chance, instead of 3/6/9/12/15%.

Sunder Armor Also increases the amount of sundered armor by 3/6/10%.

Revenge reworked;
 5 Rage, *no cooldown*
Rank 1
Instantly counterattack an enemy for 50% weapon damage + 12 to 14 damage and a high amount of threat. Revenge must follow a block, dodge or parry and can be used only once every 6 seconds.

 *6 sec internal cooldown of it's proc chance, instead of 5 sec basic ability cooldown, as it is ment to be used right after a block dodge or parry, and it being useable while on CD makes no sense conceptually.*

Improved Revenge switched position with Improved Sunder Armor (since Revenge is learned later), and reworked;
 3 ranks;
Revenge has a 10/20/30% chance to stun the target for 2 seconds and can now be used once every 5/4/3 seconds.

Improved Shield Bash compressed into 1 rank; using Shield Bash silences the target for 3 sec, and next to it a new talent, with Improved Shield Bash as a prerequisite:

Spell Reflection
 45 sec cooldown, Instant
Requires Shields
Raise your shield, reflecting the next spell cast on you. Lasts 5 sec. Can't be used with Shield Spikes.

 *A new addition to this ability is that it is only useable if your shield doesn't have Shield Spikes applied on it, and the coooldown has been increased. Alternatively, Spell Reflection could be ommited and Improved Shield Bash would remain to be 2 ranks.*

Improved Taunt switches position with One Handed Specialization, and next to Improved Taunt a new talent, with it as a prerequisite:

Incite
 1 rank
After Taunting, your next Heroic Strike, Thunder Clap or Cleave causes higher amount of threat and has increased critical hit chance by 10%.

One Handed Specialization additionally increases skill with all one handed weapons by 1/2/3/4/5.

Improved Shield Wall moved to one row below and renamed/reworked as;

Barbed Bulwark
 3 ranks
Increases the threat generated from Shield Spikes attached to your shield by 33/66/100% and increases the duration of your Shield Wall by 3/6/10 seconds.

A new talent positioned in the last row, under Barbed Bulwark and next to Shield Slam;

Indomitable
 1 Rank
Reduces the cooldown of your Intervene by 5 seconds and during Bloodrage you can use Charge while in combat.

Shield Slam costing 15 rage, 10 sec cooldown, the debuffing only occuring on a critical hit, accompanied by a knockback.

Next to it a new talent:

Improved Shield Slam
 1 rank
A succesful Revenge hit increases the critical hit chance of your next Shield Slam by 5% for 9 seconds, stacks up to 3 times.

I always thought a good way to promote shield usuage was to reward the person with bonus %threat when they block an attack. To be clear, the %threat would simply multiply your current threat against the mob by a factor (e.g. 5% --> current threat * 1.05). Thematically, I think it makes sense because having your attack blocked by a shield must be an infuriating experience.

Even with Shield Specialisation, your block chance will only ever be as high as 10%. So, the chances of getting this bonus %threat aren't great. But what if the talent also further increased your block chance as well?

So, for example:

 31point talent - Threatining Protector - increase your chance to block attacks with a shield by 10% and each successful block will increase your current threat by 10%.

So, basically, 1 in 5 attacks would give you a 10% boost to your current threat. I have no idea if that's too weak/powerful but I just like the defensive theme of this idea more than an offensive one, e.g. increasing the threat generation from your attacks.

Well, I think it's absolutely OK if there are situations where the deep prot spec does not excel at. A spec having strengths & weaknesses is good RPG design. So, in this case, the strength of a shield wearing prot warrior is when they are being focused. Conversely, they are weaker when not being focused. This weakness creates opportunities for other classes (e.g. Druid/Paladin tanks) or requires different tactics from the warrior (e.g. switch to dual wield when you aren't being focused).

Maybe it could also reduce the rage requirement instead (or both)?

This creates a rewarding moment when you block an attack and you could actually choose to shield slam an entirely different enemy (---> better threat against multiple mobs).

As you said, deep prot is useless when not focused, so it must have better ways to be focused on.

I agree that tanks of different kinds must have their pros and cons, but threat generation in single target is the main atribute of all tanks. They should deviate where their mitigation and mechanics is great with, not if they can hold threat or not...

Where the other tanks deviate?
Well,
1) Furry prot does a lot of damage (holding threat), but they recieve more damage than the other tanks. They also have some nice mechanics to avoid fear. Also they have a great rage generation.

2) Paladin is good for aoe and single targets, can bubble others to cancel their threat and must always be concerned with mana but this was heavly mitigated with teas and pots. They can remove many things bubbling theirselves, removing the bubble and re taunting. They have a good block, and dont have to swap weapons to tank multiple mobs. They also dont need to care much about hit or by having a high mitigation, since they dont use rage. Also they have blessing of freedom, they can dispell almost anything but curses on self.

3)Bear have high health pool and armor, besides can tank well 2 to 4 mobs, they can quick change forms to a quick self heal if have an oppening, they self heal in bear form also. They also can avoid some fears. Also, they dont get disarmed. And they dont block but have high dodge. Ahh yes, they also can use their shapeshift to get out of some movement impairment spells.

4) Deep prot, right now, all his mitigation is almost the same as the fury prot with a shield but with low damage, and cant hold threat. Since the furry prot can build a lead in threat then equip a shield for mitigation. They have problens with fear and aoe fights.

5) Since they are few, i dont know much about shaman tanks in Twow. But one thing i know for sure, the are damm good in making threat!

What i am trying to solve is just that, making him not a meme spec, so he can do the basic that is holding threat without doing more damage, to be viable to tank, and for that he needs more souces of bonus threat. Im fine with deep prot being a single target tanking, with low dps. They have milited anti fear mechanics, high rage thirst, greatly hit dependent and have a realy hard time hold threat.

Also, spamming shield slam would be op, do a lot of damage, make revenge less useful.

Besides that, the reward for shielding I’ve added, a reworked improved shield block, but i really think that adding more %threat when a block occurs is a great idea, and should be changed in the base stats for all tanks, not just deep prot, hell, even pallies could benefit from this.

author: Jadowsofel
subject: Demon Hunter build for Warriors
content_md:
Greetings. *I am Jadowsofel/Shaldrazath, kaldorei/sindorei disciple of <Demon Hunter>.*

This guide will lay out a basic blueprint explaining how the build works along with some conjecture filtered through personal experience. It may or may not be the first of its' kind, but I've not seen such a build elsewhere before and am posting this now only because of the many inquiries and much interest that I've encountered since I began doing dungeons & raids recently. As a new build, the possibilities are still unknown and any notion of what could be considered optimal is speculation at best. Nonetheless, I offer this guide for those drawn to creative/off-meta modes of gameplay and hope that it will serve as a semblance of proof that some degree of innovation is still possible on this old game that we all love so much. **Please experiment for yourself.**

Two quick points before I begin:

 1) I'd like to mention & thank the user Portholes (player name Iag with a capital "i") for their post entitled "Elemental Cat Build". [viewtopic.php?t=6169](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=6169) This was a catalyst of sorts which kindled the mechanical, nuts-and-bolts-level inspiration for much of this build.

 2) My calling this a demon hunter build merely reflects my own personal approach to the aesthetic & lore-derived interpretation for my gameplay. Essentially, this is a melee/magic, chaotic (proc-based) "*shadow warrior*" build.
/drink Mchealbolton/Doraexplora
As such, it can be interpreted in myriad ways depending on ones' own personal approach to aesthetics/fashion, idiosyncratic lore character background, etc. Please consider adjusting enchants and other non-essential items to best serve your own preferred manner of gameplay.  *However*. because the demon hunter was the original creative impetus that drove my efforts, I will continue to present this as a **Demon Hunter** build.

OK, so...

This is an exclusive TWoW **Rogue, Hunter and Warrior** build that, not unlike the Elemental Cat, primarily utilizes magic-damage-on-melee-hit effects to trigger the proc from the Blade of Eternal Darkness and/or
the Ornate Bloodstone Dagger. However, UNLIKE the Elemental Cat, the dual-wielding Rogue, Hunter and Warrior classes are privy to items and benefits that the Druid is not. I discovered that the weapon effect from the Blade of Eternal Darkness can be triggered by weapon enchants such as Fiery Weapon, Icy Chill and Lifestealing as well as from Shadow Oil and Dragonbreath Chili procs. Darkmoon Card: Maelstrom and Heart of Wyrmthalak can also proc the effect. Additionally, these classes can carry a bow which offers a magic-damage-on-melee-hit effect and also have access to Mail and Plate armor items that give the passive magic-damage-on-melee-hit effect as well.
Note: **The Blade of Eternal Darkness has no internal cooldown for its' weapon effect proc rate.**

See below an example of an ideal gear setup:
 
 **Armor:**
Incendosaur Skin Gloves <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60582>
Incendosaur Skin Boots <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60568>
Incendosaur Skin Pauldrons <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60572>
Lavadrenched Chainmail <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80704>
Leggings of Fiery Temper <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61505>
Thunder Lizard's Hide <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81308> (Horde-only)
Ring of Electrical Binding <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61332>
Blazefury Medallion <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17111>
 **Weapons:**
Blade of Eternal Darkness <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17780>
+
Flurry Axe <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=871>
or
Tempest's Rage <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83564>
Flamestring Bow <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80825>
 **Trinkets:**
Darkmoon Card: Maelstrom <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19289>
Heart of Wyrmthalak <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22321>
or
Hand of Justice <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=11815>
 **Consumables:**
Dragonbreath Chili <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12217>
Shadow Oil <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=3824>

Each item synergizes to maximize consistency rate of Blade of Eternal Darkness's (aka BoED's) weapon effect proc.
 **Note:** When considering your offhand weapon, I suggest focusing on weapon speed (the faster the better) and one that has an innate damage proc which may have it's own chance to proc the BoED's weapon effect.

Math has never been my forte but allow me to break this down as you consider the possibilities:
 **Blade of Eternal Darkness has a 10% chance to proc upon successful spell hit.**
 *Every successful melee strike you land will give you an additional **10** simultaneous spell hits from all of the passive magic-damage-on-melee-hit items.
 **This equates to a 65% proc rate for Blade of Eternal Darkness per successful melee strike.**
 *The 3-set bonus from the Incendosaur set grants an additional **5%** chance to land a magic attack upon successful melee strike which has it's own chance to proc the BoED weapon effect.
 *The Flurry Axe has approximately a **5-10%** chance to grant an additional strike and thus additional procs.
 *The Tempest's Rage has a **5-10%** chance to proc it's 15% haste ability. **More haste = more procs.**
 *Fiery/Icy/Lifestealing enchants have a proc rate that scales with weapon attack speed. At 1.5 this probably results in approximately a **5%** proc rate. Again, enchant procs can trigger BoED procs.
 *The Darkmoon:Maelstrom card and the Heart of Wyrmthalak both have approximately a **5%** proc rate and can themselves proc the BoED weapon effect.
 *Shadow Oil and Dragonbreath Chili both have a **5%** proc rate and can also proc the BoED.
Factoring this all together, the potential for immense burst damage becomes clear.

This brings me to my next point..

For a DPS(**Havoc**) variation of this build, I propose (presuming that +hit is sufficient) that **haste is key.**
The concept is to land as many melee strikes in as quick a succession as possible so as to land as many procs as possible. This necessarily involves eschewing traditional defensive & offensive stats such as stamina, agility and strength so as to maximize melee strike output and thus **proc output.** The majority of your damage will come from magic damage via procs - not your melee weapons. Haste provides a static boost to your weapon attack speed and auto-attack continues concurrent to any queued special ability attack. With this in mind, now consider that both the BoED and Flurry axe have a base attack speed of 1.5. **The global cooldown or GCD timer for abilities is 1.5 seconds**. This means that any haste increase will bring your base attack speed for both Boed & Flurry Axe (+12% haste for Tempest's Rage) below the GCD timer allowing for more auto-attacks to rotate on a separate, shorter timer within & during the cooldown of your primary ability attack of choice, presumably Hamstring.

See below for a list of enchants/consumables/buffs that increase your haste:

 **Enchants:**
Enchant Gloves Minor Haste <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=13948>
 **Augmentations:**
Arcanum of Rapidity <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18329>
Sigil of Quickness <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61437>
 **Buffs:**
Warchief's Blessing [https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=1 ... s-blessing](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=16609/warchiefs-blessing)
 **Consumables:**
Danonzo's Tel'Abim Medley <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60978#reward-of>
Potion of Quickness <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61181>
Juju Flurry <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12450>

There are of course many custom TWoW armor pieces that add haste as well. Mix these in wherever possible whilst ensuring that your +hit is sufficient.

Also consider that warriors have an innate method of increasing haste via Flurry 3/3 so perhaps mix agility/crit into your stat prio wherever possible.

 **As a warrior**, this build also potentially allows for a quite viable **tanking** variation where you focus on **stamina**, **agility** and/or **armor** instead of haste. This is because rapid procs can generate rapid threat. Combined with a warriors natural threat-generating abilities and the fact that the essence of this build remains intact while using a shield, it' certainly a variation to consider. Indeed, **Vengeance** (albeit shieldless) is one of the two talent specs of the demon hunter.

Now to my final point..

Another dimension to this build is the fact that both Shadow Oil (56%) and Dragonbreath Chili (100%) scale with spell power. This allows for the build to somewhat prioritize the inclusion of +spell power into the setup. Though the grind to exalted with Cenarion Circle is daunting to say the least, keep in mind that the nature of this build will allow for **perpetual uptime for the Wrath of Cenarius item proc**, further increasing the damage of the Oil & Chili. Thus, I consider this to be the other of the two BiS rings for this build.

Here's a list of some items to increase spell damage synergy:

 **Armor:**
Wrath of Cenarius <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=21190>
 **Consumables:**
Dreamtonic <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61423>
Greater Arcane Elixir <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13454>
Flask of Supreme Spellpower <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13512>
Gilneas Hot Stew <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=84041>
Gift of Arthas <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=9088>

 **Doubtless there will be items and consumables, some finite, that I've missed but the information and lists above will at least provide a reasonably attainable basis for players to strive for that can bring this build to life.**

Here I offer an approach to talents for both DPS (**Havoc**) and tanking (**Vengeance**). As stated several times already, I implore you to **experiment** and **create** a style that best suits **your own** manner of gameplay.
This is only a suggestion:

 **Havoc:** <https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior/52-5515WU6H6-5C>
 **Vengeance:** <https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior/50U1-0-5HV3XK15>

I'm happy to share this guide with the server and hope that it might **inspire** you to try it yourself and even consider playing this build as a glaive-wielding kalorei or sin'dorei demon hunter too, or, better yet, **inspire** you to **innovate** a **new** build or approach to gameplay of **your own**.

 */bow*

Heart of Wyrmthalak https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22321
or
Hand of Justice https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=11815
Consumables:
Dragonbreath Chili https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12217
Shadow Oil https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=3824

Each item synergizes to maximize consistency rate of Blade of Eternal Darkness's (aka BoED's) weapon effect proc.
Note: When considering your offhand weapon, I suggest focusing on weapon speed (the faster the better) and one that has an innate damage proc which may have it's own chance to proc the BoED's weapon effect.

Math has never been my forte but allow me to break this down as you consider the possibilities:
Blade of Eternal Darkness has a 10% chance to proc upon successful spell hit.
*Every successful melee strike you land will give you an additional 10 simultaneous spell hits from all of the passive magic-damage-on-melee-hit items.
This equates to a 65% proc rate for Blade of Eternal Darkness per successful melee strike.
*The 3-set bonus from the Incendosaur set grants an additional 5% chance to land a magic attack upon successful melee strike which has it's own chance to proc the BoED weapon effect.
*The Flurry Axe has approximately a 5-10% chance to grant an additional strike and thus additional procs.
*The Tempest's Rage has a 5-10% chance to proc it's 15% haste ability. More haste = more procs.
*Fiery/Icy/Lifestealing enchants have a proc rate that scales with weapon attack speed. At 1.5 this probably results in approximately a 5% proc rate. Again, enchant procs can trigger BoED procs.
*The Darkmoon:Maelstrom card and the Heart of Wyrmthalak both have approximately a 5% proc rate and can themselves proc the BoED weapon effect.
*Shadow Oil and Dragonbreath Chili both have a 5% proc rate and can also proc the BoED.
Factoring this all together, the potential for immense burst damage becomes clear.

This brings me to my next point..

For a DPS(Havoc) variation of this build, I propose (presuming that +hit is sufficient) that haste is key.
The concept is to land as many melee strikes in as quick a succession as possible so as to land as many procs as possible. This necessarily involves eschewing traditional defensive & offensive stats such as stamina, agility and strength so as to maximize melee strike output and thus proc output. The majority of your damage will come from magic damage via procs - not your melee weapons. Haste provides a static boost to your weapon attack speed and auto-attack continues concurrent to any queued special ability attack. With this in mind, now consider that both the BoED and Flurry axe have a base attack speed of 1.5. The global cooldown or GCD timer for abilities is 1.5 seconds. This means that any haste increase will bring your base attack speed for both Boed & Flurry Axe (+12% haste for Tempest's Rage) below the GCD timer allowing for more auto-attacks to rotate on a separate, shorter timer within & during the cooldown of your primary ability attack of choice, presumably Hamstring.

See below for a list of enchants/consumables/buffs that increase your haste:

Enchants:
Enchant Gloves Minor Haste https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=13948
Augmentations:
Arcanum of Rapidity https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18329
Sigil of Quickness https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61437
Buffs:
Warchief's Blessing https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=1 ... s-blessing
Consumables:
Danonzo's Tel'Abim Medley https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60978#reward-of
Potion of Quickness https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61181
Juju Flurry https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12450

There are of course many custom TWoW armor pieces that add haste as well. Mix these in wherever possible whilst ensuring that your +hit is sufficient.

Also consider that warriors have an innate method of increasing haste via Flurry 3/3 so perhaps mix agility/crit into your stat prio wherever possible.

As a warrior, this build also potentially allows for a quite viable tanking variation where you focus on stamina, agility and/or armor instead of haste. This is because rapid procs can generate rapid threat. Combined with a warriors natural threat-generating abilities and the fact that the essence of this build remains intact while using a shield, it' certainly a variation to consider. Indeed, Vengeance (albeit shieldless) is one of the two talent specs of the demon hunter.

Now to my final point..

Another dimension to this build is the fact that both Shadow Oil (56%) and Dragonbreath Chili (100%) scale with spell power. This allows for the build to somewhat prioritize the inclusion of +spell power into the setup. Though the grind to exalted with Cenarion Circle is daunting to say the least, keep in mind that the nature of this build will allow for perpetual uptime for the Wrath of Cenarius item proc, further increasing the damage of the Oil & Chili. Thus, I consider this to be the other of the two BiS rings for this build.

Here's a list of some items to increase spell damage synergy:

Armor:
Wrath of Cenarius https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=21190
Consumables:
Dreamtonic https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61423
Greater Arcane Elixir https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13454
Flask of Supreme Spellpower https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13512
Gilneas Hot Stew https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=84041
Gift of Arthas https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=9088

Doubtless there will be items and consumables, some finite, that I've missed but the information and lists above will at least provide a reasonably attainable basis for players to strive for that can bring this build to life.

Here I offer an approach to talents for both DPS (Havoc) and tanking (Vengeance). As stated several times already, I implore you to experiment and create a style that best suits your own manner of gameplay.
This is only a suggestion:

Havoc: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior/52-5515WU6H6-5C
Vengeance: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior/50U1-0-5HV3XK15

I'm happy to share this guide with the server and hope that it might inspire you to try it yourself and even consider playing this build as a glaive-wielding kalorei or sin'dorei demon hunter too, or, better yet, inspire you to innovate a new build or approach to gameplay of your own.

/bow

Here's one I use all the time.  It allows use of Revenge/Bloodrage/Shield Block to be used automatically when its off CD and you have the rage to use them.  Also, the taunt will activate automatically when a mob isnt targeting you.

/run if not UnitIsUnit('player', 'targettarget') then CastSpellByName('Taunt'); end

/cast Bloodrage

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Two Hand Slam Viable?
content_md:
From patchnotes for 1.17.2 regarding 2h slammer.
> Slam is now taught at level 14 and pauses your weapon swing timer instead of resetting it.

Also, rage generation formula has been changed to relieve rage starvation.
> While Vanilla’s system shines for late 60 raiders, unfortunately everywhere else, players are harshly punished and suffering rage-starvation, especially for:
>  Levelers that don’t have the absolute greatest weapon possible.
>  Dungeoneers and fresh raiders, in fights where you are unable to offtank for the added rage income.
>  When dueling the more heavily armored (and especially shield wearing) player classes.
>  We do recognize the enjoyment found in top-end raiding, and we aim to retain a similar game-feel there. To retain this, and relieve the widespread pain points above, we find that a new rage generation formula that's calculated 90% depending on your gear and 10% of it is predetermined based on your weapon speed best helps achieve this. With the formula change, players will notice significantly increased rage generation in these cases. The top is the same, but the bottom has been raised up.

Improved Slam is now in Arms tree.
So now you have variety in builds.

First is [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior? ... AAAAAAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior?points=dQQAAYDQpaAYAAAoAooACAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA%3D)
You slam+sweeping strikes if boss has more than 20% of health and start spamming Execute when boss  health is lower.

or you can go for Death Wish instead of Execute
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior? ... AAAAAAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior?points=dQQAAYDQpCAAAAAoAogYAoBAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA%3D)

Hamstring now has a cooldown, so you can't force procs by spamming it.
Windfury has changed - you can use sharpening stones along with WF, but you don't get bonus attack power for extra attack.

New ability to spam to trigger procs officially is Sunder Armor
> Sunder Armor's rage cost has been reduced from 15 to 10 rage.
>
>  Developer Comment: These changes were done to reduce Warrior's stickiness in player combat while elevating Sunder Armor as a tool to trigger weapon effects in its place.

Levelers that don’t have the absolute greatest weapon possible.
Dungeoneers and fresh raiders, in fights where you are unable to offtank for the added rage income.
When dueling the more heavily armored (and especially shield wearing) player classes.
We do recognize the enjoyment found in top-end raiding, and we aim to retain a similar game-feel there. To retain this, and relieve the widespread pain points above, we find that a new rage generation formula that's calculated 90% depending on your gear and 10% of it is predetermined based on your weapon speed best helps achieve this. With the formula change, players will notice significantly increased rage generation in these cases. The top is the same, but the bottom has been raised up.
Improved Slam is now in Arms tree.
So now you have variety in builds.

First is https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior? ... AAAAAAA%3D
You slam+sweeping strikes if boss has more than 20% of health and start spamming Execute when boss health is lower.

or you can go for Death Wish instead of Execute
https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior? ... AAAAAAA%3D

Hamstring now has a cooldown, so you can't force procs by spamming it.
Windfury has changed - you can use sharpening stones along with WF, but you don't get bonus attack power for extra attack.

New ability to spam to trigger procs officially is Sunder Armor
Sunder Armor's rage cost has been reduced from 15 to 10 rage.

Developer Comment: These changes were done to reduce Warrior's stickiness in player combat while elevating Sunder Armor as a tool to trigger weapon effects in its place.

author: Czasku
subject: Re: Whirlwind axe
content_md:
The short answer is simple; Big weapon = big whack on puny hummie.

The long answer: When you level up there's lack of critical strike for warriors, you usually run with 5% which isn't much. But at lvl 30 you can take Axe Specialization which is additional 5%, the mace specialization isn't very good tbh because in vanilla it doesnt generate any rage (in tbc they buffed it to grant you 7 rage when it procs making it the decent alternative to axe spec) and the sword spec is 5% flat extra swing chance (it surpasses the axe spec when you have at least 25% base chance to crit because the extra swing can also crit) also when you get lvl 45 you can get Cruelty that adds another 5% giving you flat 15% chance to critically strike making your Impale and Deep Wounds proc more often.

When you're lvl 40 you get Mortal Strike, your only one instant damaging ability on demand (you wont have enough rage to also use Whirlwind, trust me.) so you want it to hit hard. The dps of 2.6 and 3.6 weapon speed may be the same, BUT Mortal Strike has 6 seconds cooldown, so its damage will be bigger with slow weapon than with fast weapon. Blizz stated that they wanted people in vanilla to change they playstyle based on weapon speed, thats why there's so many "next melee" abilities in vanilla.

So, in summary:
Whirlwind Axe is boosting your only one instant damage ability and gives you extra source of rage and damage from Impale, Deep Wounds AND potential strike from Overpower.
Whirlwind Sword boosts your Heroic Strike and gives you potential extra strike (which is obviously extra source of rage) its also probably better for 2h fury.
Whirlwind Mace is something between, but without extra source of rage generation. It also gives you swag because no one is using it.

author: Zulnam
subject: Re: Should i pla Warrior or Druid?
content_md:
druid can tank most bosses in raids.

The only real downside when compared to warrior is that you need to already be somewhat geared, where as warriors are the go-to tank for progression raids. even in mostly blue gear they can still tank most of the MC bosses and their tier set is specifically built for tanking, making it much easier to gear up and progress the raid.

In contrast druid tank gearing is still a bit awkward (leaps better than vanilla tho), so you will have to run some raids first as OT or dps and gear up that way.

Also your main raids for gearing are different: where a wariior can get pretty good tanking gear from MC, druid has to focus on AQ20. And many of your BiS items for tanking are still blue items (see discord druid channel pins for list of gear).

As for hitcap, warrior can probably reach it easier than druid imo. If you go human you will also get like 3% hit from the weapon skill but keep in mind these are subject to change in the upcoming major patch, so i would not choose a human warrior now for the weapon skill racial alone.

author: Manletow
subject: Warriors in PVP (Updated for CC2)
content_md:
View my first thread for context: [viewtopic.php?t=10856](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=10856)

My primary personal recommendation to elevate Warrior was to give them Spell Reflect + Shattering Throw.
This would have brought Warrior from an 'F' grade up to a 'D-'.
That would technically be a passing grade.
Note: Warrior is already extremely popular and dominates in PVE. It's fair for it to be mediocre in PVP.

Anyway, obviously those abilities were not implemented.
So what important skills (in regards to PVP) **did** Warriors receive?

Arms:
 1. 2 yards extra melee range. (Polearms exclusive)
This is excellent -- allows a "Master of Arms" to actually clown on other melee.
Previously they just went toe-to-toe against other melee and still lost 50% of the time. It was a farce.
Now you Hamstring then keep at 7 yards distance to literally dunk on them.

 2. Having Pummel in Battle Stance is much needed.
Previously had to use Shield Bash which was not realistic for obvious reasons.
Not sure how the 'daze' mechanic (if Talented) is going to be useful but whatever -- an interrupt is a blessing!!

Note: Counterattack is awful. Does poor damage and the effect is useless.
You will only use this attack against other melee so the 'root' is somewhat irrelevant.
I guess with Polearms you can troll them at 7 yards distance as I explained. Kek.

Fury:
Blood Craze has been buffed to WoTLK levels of power-creep.
This may be the number 1 most impactful change as this allows the solo Warrior actually noteworthy amounts of self-sustaining healing.
Staying alive longer is absolutely essential for Warriors success.
Longer life = more rage = more kills = more wins

Protection:
 1. Generally they have had their god awful damage somewhat increased.
 2. And they can (reliably) dispel a Magic Effect.

TL:DR:
Warriors got a very conservative/modest power boost so the status quo will remain largely the same.
They are going from F grade to F+

Still Trash Tier i'm afraid.   maintenance_turtle
Sorry Warrior mains!

Additional Notes:
At least Paladin (which 'Hard Countered' Warrior) was hugely nerfed. So you will no longer auto-lose these fights.
Hamstring was OP due to its extremely long 15 sec debuff duration. It's fine that it has a 6 second CD now.
Orc 'Anti Stun' Racial nerf means Charge/Intercept are slightly less awful. They might actually serve their function!!

author: Xudo
subject: 10-19 warrior build 1.17.2
content_md:
Not going to pretend for perfect build. Just my thoughts to figure out build for myself.
I will list talents from best to worst with my reasoning.

Bad news. All classes can remove slow with Insignia trinket. It used to remove slow only for warrior/hunter/shaman.
Hamstring has CD. We can't spam it to proc Fiery Weapon/Crusader. Sunder Armor and Rend doesn't seem to proc fiery weapon.
Wing Clip has CD 3 sec. We will probably be kited by hunters. Though we already were kited, because 40% slow of Hamstring vs 50% slow of Wing Clip allows them to get away.

Good news. We no longer need shield to interrupt enemies! Pummel can be learned at lvl 18 and it is available in Arms.
Hamstring has CD. We are no longer stuck in melee when we engage other warrior.
We have plenty of rage. I did few duels and my rage bar was full. On lvl 19 white attack for 100 damage grant ~18 rage, white attack for 60 damage grant 10 rage.

Talents

 1. Tactical Mastery
> You retain 5/10/15/20/25 of your rage points when you change stances.

It is on 1st row, so we don't need to choose between 3 bad talents in Arms.
I surely pick Tactical mastery atleast 4 points to be able to use Disarm (20 rage) when I need it.

 2. Booming Voice
> Increases the area of effect of all shouts by 12/24/36/48/60% and the duration of your Battle and Demoralizing Shout by 12/24/36/48/60%

Our Demoralizing Shout can break rogues stealth. It is very typical situation when I approach to rogue, he stealthes. I use Bloodrage (to prevent Sap) and then Demoralizing Shout to try to break stealth. Sometimes it is successful.
Basic radius of Demo Shout is 10 yards. With 1 point it is 11 yards. So I guess with 5 points it will be 10+60%=16 yards. Now when we don't need to invest a lot to get Tactical Mastery, we can invest in Booming Voice.

 3. Improved Charge
> Increases the amount of rage generated by your Charge ability by 5/10.

Require 5 points in Arms and you can reach them with Tactical Mastery.
Rage generation was changed, so I am not sure if it is good idea.
Default Charge generates 9 range. Most of our abilities require 10 range. But you usually immediately deal melee attack on that enemy after the charge.
So at least 1 point in this talent will be useful to be sure that you get enough rage for Hamstring or Pummel if your miss/dodge/parry/absorb your initial melee attack.

 4. Improved Bloodrage
> Increases the instant Rage generated by your Bloodrage ability by 5/10.

Default Bloodrage grants you 10 rage, which is enough for macroses like "Bloodrage+Pummel" or "Bloodrage+Shield Bash" or "Bloodrage + Hamstring".
This talent is just better than Shield Specialisation to reach Iron Will.

 5. Anticipation
> Increases your Defense skill by 7/14/20.

The only good thing that this talent work regardless of your weapon. 20 of defense skill is -0.8% to be critically hit and 0.8% to block, parry, dodge.
It also better than Shield Specialisation to reach Iron Will.

 6. Iron Will
> Increases your chance to resist Stun And Charm effects by an additional 3/6/9/12/15%.

There are a lot of stuns on 10-19. Hammer of Justice, War Stomp, Grenades, Charge stun, Improved Concussive Shot, Impact (though fire mages are rare find), Blackout (though I rarely see priests in shadow).
So I think it is useful talent. The only downside of it that it requires you to spend all 10 talents to stun resistance, so you don't get Tactical Mastery.
You lose ability to quickly switch to Disarm. Though you can use it after Bloodrage and any melee attack.
You also lose additional 5-6 yards of Demo Shout.

 7. Cruelty
> Increases your chance to get a critical strike with melee weapons by 1/2/3/4/5%

 1% of crit per point. Plain simple useful.

 8. Deflection
> Increases your Parry chance by 1/2/3/4/5%

Parrying the attack allows your next melee attack to land earlier. You need to face enemies to parry. It is hard to successfully play with it in real situations.

 9. Improved Thunder Clap
> Reduces the cost of your Thunder Clap ability by 1/2/4 rage point and increases the damage by 20/40/60%

It costs 20 rage and deals 17 damage untalented. Might be a good button to debuff enemy melees. Reduced cost allows to press it earlier.

 10. Dual wield Specialization
> Increases the damage done by your offhand weapon by 5/10/15/20/25% and your chance to hit with your offhand weapon by 2/4/6/8/10%.

The only reason I will equip offhand is to get immune disarm effect from Steel weapon chain while keeping Fiery Weapon enchant on main hand weapon. This situation occurs only when I charge to another warrior. I don't think I need damage nor hit chance for offhand in this situation.
I don't think it is useful for pvp.

 11. Unbridled wrath
> Gives you a 15/30/45/60/75% chance to generate an additional Rage point when you deal melee damage with a weapon. The effect is doubled for two-handed weapons.

You will have plenty of rage in PvP without this talent. I don't think it is useful.

 12. Shield Specialization.
> Increases your chance to block attacks with a shield by 1/2/3/4/5% and generates 1/2/3/4/5 rage when a block occurs.

I don't think it is useful for PvP at all.

 13. Improved Heroic Strike
> Reduces the cost of your Heroic Strike ability by 1 rage point.

It is "Next melee" attack, which increases damage of next strike by 32. Might be useful to dump rage, but I don't think it is reasonable to spend talents here.

 14. Improved Rend
> Increases the bleed damage done by your Rend ability by 10/20%.

Rend costs 10 rage, deals "28 damage over 12 sec". It is 4 ticks on rank 2.
Rend also scales with attack power. On lvl 19 I have 50 strength and 137 attack power without gear. Untalented Rend deals 13 damage per tick (52 damage total). When I equip my (not perfect) gear I have 96 strength or 229 attack power. Rend ticks for 18 damage (72 damage total).
+10% of damage will be equal to 18+10%=19.8=19 or 18+20%=21,6=21 damage.
I usually use Rend on rogues after Hamstring to get away from them and force them to stay out of stealth.
 1 or 3 additional points of damage does not look like good reason to spec into it. At least for PvP, at least on 19 lvl.
I will probably use it more than before, because I have spare GCD, but not always because it break sheep.

 15. Toughness
> Increases your armor value from items by 2% and the amount of damage absorbed by your shield by 3%

In my (not perfect) gear with shield I have 1452 armor. It is 41.9% to reduce incoming physical damage.
Additional 150 armor will reduce incoming physical damage for 2-3%. I don't think I notice the difference on 10-19. It will be like 1 or 2 damage points.
Other downside is that if you get Toughness, you don't get Tactical Mastery, Booming Voice and Iron Will.

Conclusion
I end up with two builds:
 1. Tactical Mastery+Booming Voice [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior? ... AAAAAAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior?points=FAIAAAAAAAAAAAEAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA%3D)
It has ability to switch from Battle Stance and immediately use Disarm.
It allows to Hamstring even if your melee attack miss.
It has improved area to break rogues stealth.
 2. Iron Will [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior? ... AAAAAAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior?points=AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAQYFAAAAAAAAAAAA%3D)
 15% to resist Hammer of Justice, War Stomp, Grenades and Improved Concussive Shot proc.

author: Webmaster
subject: SuperMacro Warrior Leveling Rend, Battle Shout, Target Nearest, etc
content_md:
I think you might like this simple, but efficient supermacro with a few conditional checks.
Code: Select all

```
/run if UnitIsDead("target") and UnitExists("target") then ClearTarget(); end
/run if GetUnitName("target")==nil then TargetNearestEnemy() end

/run for i=1,120 do if IsCurrentAction(i) then return end end CastSpellByName("Attack")

/cast Charge

/run local i,x=1,0 while UnitDebuff("target",i) do if UnitDebuff("target",i)=="Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Gouge" then x=1 end i=i+1 end if x==0 and UnitHealth("target")/UnitHealthMax("target") > 0.3 then CastSpellByName("Rend") end

/run local hasBuff=false for i=1,40 do if UnitBuff("player",i) and strfind(UnitBuff("player",i),"Warrior_BattleShout") then hasBuff=true break end end if not hasBuff then CastSpellByName("Battle Shout(Rank 1)") end

/cast Heroic Strike
```

author: Yasara
subject: Re: Newbie wow player warrior leveling
content_md:
Here a classic armsbuild for leveling:
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior? ... AAAAAAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/warrior?points=DQFARYDQpYAABABoAoBYAoAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA%3D)

"Rotation": charge -> sunder amor (which is often better than heroic strike) -> rend and sunder armor again. Execute is situational because starting a new fight (after killing an enemy with execute) with 0 rage and charge on CD is lame. While leveling Overpower is very OP and it proccs really often. Counterattack ist also very usefull while leveling (thats why both are skilled/upgraded in the guide above). And keep your Battle Shout up.

Your stats are stamina + strengh an you play with a 2handweapon. Try to keep your weapon up2date because they are everything for warrior. Make sure your weapons are as slow as possible. Also have a shield and a fast 1handweapon (speed 1,x) rdy because when you go in dungeons you often have to tank (or to off-tank) or you need it for outside elite grp quests.

Try to do quests where the enemys are 2-3 levels below your own level and you can't really die. You also only have to eat every 4-6 mob this way. Quests with mobs with the same level are often a pain in the ass. And try to fight mobs 1 vs 1. Warriors hate fighting outnumbered (for example you can use Overpower and Counterattack only vs. mobs who parried you - but you don't know which mob it was and so you have to tab through the mobs)

Macro

For my basic abilities I use a simple startattack macro like

#showtooltip Rend
/startattack
/cast Rend

#showtooltip sunder armor
/startattack
/cast sunder armor

They are other usefull macros (for example for switching your 2handweapon into 1hand + shield) but I don't use them atm. You find them here or with google.

When you omit the spellrank in a macro the macro always choose the highest rank available.

Warriors hate fighting outnumbered (for example you can use Overpower and Counterattack only vs. mobs who parried you - but you don't know which mob it was and so you have to tab through the mobs)

Macro

For my basic abilities I use a simple startattack macro like

#showtooltip Rend
/startattack
/cast Rend

#showtooltip sunder armor
/startattack
/cast sunder armor

They are other usefull macros (for example for switching your 2handweapon into 1hand + shield) but I don't use them atm. You find them here or with google.

When you omit the spellrank in a macro the macro always choose the highest rank available.

People were already talking about it 20 years ago*. Hamstring kiting is great against higher level opponents but completely unsuitable for normal leveling, in my personal opinion.

 1) When you start a fight, you'll get at least two attacks from enemies before you're out of range (due to latency alone). Most enemies (especially animals) have a much higher attack speed than you do. And by the time you are out of range, the time is almost up and you have to approach the mob again.

 2) Unnecessarily complicated (especially for beginners like the TE).
 - You have to practise running sideways away from opponents and not pummeling other opponents. In the worst case, you also pull the enemy away from the group of quest mobs and then have to run back (you have to kite several times during a fight; or you kite back but then you get even more attacks)
 - For this to really work you have to play with a swing timer addon and really look at it all the time. I find that _much_ too stressful for simple leveling.

 3) Overpower (and now Counterattack) do not benefit from this playstil.

 4) Due to the reduced rage generation (due to the lack of incoming damage from enemy attacks) you often have only autoattacks.

author: Neechy
subject: Make Shield Warriors Great Again
content_md:
Were they ever great in vanilla? Not really, but the title is catchy.

Point is, even with recent class changes the player consensus seems to be that Deep Prot is still not that great in PvE.

 **Request to devs: Please make sword and board playstyle more viable for tanking.** A heavy armored warrior with a shield is like the class fantasy prototype. IMO this seems like the type of character you would want protecting you when going up against a powerful raid boss or being swarmed by multiple enemies.. So the fact that DW warriors continues to be the meta for tanking is disappointing to say the least. I mean the very idea that a warrior swinging two weapons around crazily would somehow provide better protection than a dude with a bigass shield seems pretty bizarre.

And I think the devs' idea with these class changes was to make deep prot more enticing, but with all the player complaints, it seems that the goal has fallen short...

I'm not sure exactly what it would take in order for shield prot to be a more optimal tank so I am interested to hear from others.

One possible suggestion:
New talent: 'Damage Shield'
 - Deep in the Protection Tree to advocate for shield specialization
 - **2 talent points: On a successful block, you reflect [10/20]% of the enemy's damage back to them. This damage deals a high amount of threat.**
 - The idea is that by using a shield you could start doing more comparable damage and threat as DW warriors, thereby reducing the need for tanks to go the DW rout
 - Example scenario: A raid boss hits you for 5000 damage and receives 1000 damage back (assuming 0 armor). May not seem like a lot but it adds up the higher your block %.
 - And because it is based only on successful blocks and only on the damage of the enemy, it is a very PvE focused talent that shouldn't be OP in PvP against other players.

IMO this seems like the type of character you would want protecting you when going up against a powerful raid boss or being swarmed by multiple enemies.. So the fact that DW warriors continues to be the meta for tanking is disappointing to say the least. author: Graftington
subject: Re: Make Shield Warriors Great Again
content_md:
I recently started leveling a warrior (first time for classic) so my experience is mostly limited to low levels. But I have played a warrior in other expansions. I know people have worries about power creep but I think most of us are here for the PvE and leveling experience. So I think that should always take precedent over pvp "balance" - my argument is no one makes it to end game to raid or pvp if the leveling experience turns them off. I think the turtle devs do a really good job of keeping things minimal / small in number but those little tweaks matter.

I think it would be really helpful if shield slam was a much earlier and core ability (level 20 or so?) to let prot warriors actually have a use for their shield in combat. This is such an iconic ability and core to the class fantasy. It would help low level tanking and get players used to using it (and a shield and D stance). You can even make it a lesser version just doing damage and threat (no dispel or block) until higher levels. I also find with the new rage generation that I don't have an effective rage dump - heroic strike is too slow so having a nice 20 rage shield slam would give me something to do.

I know classic is all about spirit but having something like blood crazy be innate (or higher in the tree) or victory rush for "honor or experience kill" like most other classes get would really help with leveling. I have always been a proponent of increasing out of combat regen or food/drink - waiting around isn't fun for anyone.

I have always liked the shield and reflect / thorns model for tanking and it feels really bad that paladins and druids get this innately yet warriors do not. Belt buckles are certainly a welcome addition but I am not sure why they are so spaced out just like shield spikes. Why don't we have a copper and bronze shield spike to help low level warriors? Also probably most controversial take here but I think a shield spike should work like thorns and always proc on getting hit not just when the warrior blocks. (given that this version of shield block is 1 hit only)

If you've never played a guardian (tank warrior) in LOTRO I highly recommend giving it a go - it is one of my favorite versions of a tank and I'd love to see some of that flavor make its way into the turtle wow warrior design.

author: krylorandrax
subject: Re: Make Shield Warriors Great Again
content_md:
There are two very separate issues with Warrior tanking now, each of which needs a different solution;

 1. As an MT
It is specifically threat from the normal Deep-Prot rotation when compared to the other tanks (Druid/Pally/Shaman) that needs an update. A solution that would fit into the tanking style of Deep-Prot would be to have the effect from Reprisal (Row 5) reset the CD of Shield-Slam and make it cost 5 rage (rather than 20). This would encourage the intended play-style.

 2. As an OT
This one is much more difficult as the other tanks (Druid/Pally/Shaman/FProt) have a reasonably stable method of generating threat without taking dmg. The solution for this needs to be very far down the Prot tree (possibly capstone) so that it does not impact other warrior DPS builds (including FProt). On the basis that a 1H+Shield OT is not generating a lot of rage the solution would need to allow threat for little/zero cost so that it could sustain reasonable threat generation while not actively tanking. As much as I disliked it, after trying many times, Blizzard themselves determined that Vigilance was mathematically good enough as a solution.

The TWow version ("Beware the old soldier") would need to also work with the updated play-style from (1) above. One possible version, working similar to the Paladin Hand of Sacrifice)  could transfer a fixed % (1-2%) of dmg done from the target (MT) to the Warrior. This would help generate an acceptable amount of rage that the Deep-Prot war could then use their normal play-style, benefiting from (1) above.

[edit: replicated this suggestion over to the dedicated forum: [viewtopic.php?t=16202](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=16202)]

author: bonefire1
subject: When will Warrior receive nerfs? [rant]
content_md:
Honestly, I'm tired of these entitled Warrior players.

Best DPS class, best TANK class, best PVE class overall, does pretty great in PVP as well, is nearly unstoppable when paired with a healer although it's argued that's the case for every class...

Leveling is insanely fast, probably the fastest in the game because of how many dungeons you can get into.

Best hybrid class in the game. Doesn't matter if you opt to be either a TANK or DPS, either way you are tanky and you do great dmg(at no cost/tradeoffs), no matter the role you want to pick.

It's the most broken class in the game, making you really shake your head when playing with another class unless you want to be a healer, do pvp or rp.

With recent class changes, the situation has gotten better, otherwise in the past you were just told/mocked, why don't you pick Warrior, why don't you just play with Warrior?

Now these entitled people have the nerve to ask for further class improvements? It's like it's never enough for them, they want every single thing to be as overpowered and perfect as possible.

Warrior players want so many buffs, might as well remove every other single class from the game and give Warrior an op healing spec as well, then it can really do it all.

The mods really need to do something about these Warrior buff posts. Maybe nerf Warrior to the ground in order to make them realize what they really had going on.

I cannot imagine the rage from them, knowing their class is no longer the best in DPS, tanking or the best hybrid class.

Either Warrior needs to be nerfed or other classes need to be buffed more, otherwise at some point, players will start leaving or mocking Warrior players as a no skill op meta class player.

Then they also have the nerve to go to other class changes threads and demand nerfs for other classes, specs, "oh Warrior doesn't have this but this class does? That's unfair, Warrior must have also!".

As a solution, buffing other classes wouldn't quite work well because I've already seen plenty of powercreep posts...

Okay my rant is now over, I had to create an account just for this post. I've been with the server since the start and never really posted anything but I had to let my feelings out at least once. I know many people agree with me, even if in silence.

And for other classes out there, I feel you! I think it's just a lore thing or a stigma for Warriors to be the best class in WoW.

author: Atompapst
subject: Re: Macro help
content_md:
Code: Select all

```
/run local a, b, c, d, e = GetShapeshiftFormInfo(3) DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:AddMessage("icon: " .. tostring(a) .. " name: " .. tostring(b) .. " active: " .. tostring(c) .. " castable: " .. tostring(d) .. " id: " .. tostring(e))
```

This will give you information about every Stance you are currently in and not

 1 = Battle Stance
 2 = Defensive Stance
 3 = Beserker Stance

based on the value active you can ask if active == 1 and then use CastSpellByName("Spell Name")
content_html:
Code: Select all

/run local a, b, c, d, e = GetShapeshiftFormInfo(3) DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:AddMessage("icon: " .. tostring(a) .. " name: " .. tostring(b) .. " active: " .. tostring(c) .. " castable: " .. tostring(d) .. " id: " .. tostring(e))

1 = Battle Stance
2 = Defensive Stance
3 = Beserker Stance

author: Captain4k
subject: Warrior Envy is Nonsensical [Rant]
content_md:
How do people hate on warriors out of all 9 classes? It's the equivalent of being born in a privileged class and hating on the successful guy that came from nothing and earned everything he has, despite not having the same advantages in life. And it's clearly people with a very specific type of entitled ego that envy warriors because anyone who's levelled a warrior knows that it's one of, if not the most difficult class to not only reach level cap with, but to play exceptionally well due to how heavily gear dependant they are.

We all know that TWoW is strict on the preservation of Blizzard's blueprint of class identity. What is the warriors class identity? Simple answer: A high risk, high reward raging berserker. Tanking aside, high damage is LITERALLY the value that warriors are expected to provide to groups and raids. Because if a warrior is not providing high damage benefits to your party, what else are they useful for? So if damage is the main expectation of the class, OBVIOUSLY it's going to exceed exceptionally well in that role, *as intended by the designers of the class.*

Okay, since warriors are "so overpowered" and this is clearly the oppression olympics, lets compare and contrast warrior benefits to every other class in the game:

Can a warrior have the highest damage performance- Yes
Can a warrior heal themselves with spells?  - No
Can a warrior heal others for a short time after death? - No
Can a warrior resurrect a fallen teammate? - No
Can a warrior resurrect themselves? - No
Can a warrior summon other teammates to the location? - No
Can a warrior make portals to teleport themselves or teammates? - No
Can a warrior shape-shift and fulfill every role in the game? - No
Can a warrior stealth at will or easily escape combat - No
Can a warrior AoE farm by making it rain icicle spears or fireballs from the sky? - No
Can a warrior banish or polymorph targets? - No
Can a warrior set traps for targets? - No
Can a warrior grant levitate or slow fall to themselves or others? - No
Can a warrior walk on water or grant underwater breathing? - No
Can a warrior turn into a cheetah or wolf for increased movement speed? - No
Can a warrior grant Aspect of the Pack or Cheetah for increased movement speed?  - No
Can a warrior tame pets or summon demons to aide them in combat? - No
Can a warrior grant a variety of buffs to party or raid members? - No

So then what significant value does a warrior provide to a party, you ask?  The answer is damage. High freaking damage. And yet people hate on the warrior class for shining in the one single area that it excels at, despite it lacking in virtually every other aspect of class benefit comparatively. With that being considered, if every class were to be equal to warriors in terms of damage, then wtf would be the incentive to play a warrior over any other class?

P.S. Don't even try the "Warriors are the best tanks" argument. Warriors **WERE** the "best" tanks because vanilla WoW was released half-baked due to the time constraints of its development cycle. It wasn't intended for them to be the only viable tank class. TWoW has since rectified that issue with the Class Changes 2 patch. So all tanks are now viable and each uniquely excel in areas that are specific to their class.
