author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Warrior Envy is Nonsensical [Rant]
content_md:
Levelling in wow is never hard. Even the biggest muppet can get a warrior on hc to level 60 by exclusively grinding green mobs/grey quests. There is absolutely no deserved benefits just for making it to a class that is slightly more difficault than the rest to level if you dont know the game.
If you do know the game and you keep your gear up to date by frequent dungeonruns you get instant access to because you can click "Tank" warrior levelling is not only easy but also quick.
Saying you are the underdog who made it sounds like "i got a small loan of a million dollars"

I love how you list out all kinds of niche things other classes can do that have zero raid applications but conviniently leave out all the good things warriors can and regularly do in raids.

 - can warrior kick reliably with less sacrifice to their dps than mages, warlocks, rogues, druids and arguably shamans? - Yes x4
 - can warriors completely disarm any dangerous aoe situation with ae taint & lip, even as dps with no gear? - Yes
 - Can warrior not only deal the highest single target in the game but also excel in dps when fighting multiple enemies - Yes
 - Can warriors survive more cleave damage than any other dps class Yes- except arguably paladin
 - Can DPS warriors just save the raid by tanking any trashnob just in dps gear? - Yes

While i dont necessarily think warriors need huge nerf or that every other spec needs to be able to compete with warrior in all the meteics he excels at, warriors thinking they are the underdog dps that made it is peak comedy

But on the tank argument, you are sadly right, paladin and druid are grossly overbuffed and should get nerfed back down

content_html:
How do people hate on warriors out of all 9 classes? It's the equivalent of being born in a privileged class and hating on the successful guy that came from nothing and earned everything he has, despite not having the same advantages in life. And it's clearly people with a very specific type of entitled ego that envy warriors because anyone who's levelled a warrior knows that it's one of, if not the most difficult class to not only reach level cap with, but to play exceptionally well due to how heavily gear dependant they are.

We all know that TWoW is strict on the preservation of Blizzard's blueprint of class identity. What is the warriors class identity? Simple answer: A high risk, high reward raging berserker. Tanking aside, high damage is LITERALLY the value that warriors are expected to provide to groups and raids. Because if a warrior is not providing high damage benefits to your party, what else are they useful for? So if damage is the main expectation of the class, OBVIOUSLY it's going to exceed exceptionally well in that role, as intended by the designers of the class.

Okay, since warriors are "so overpowered" and this is clearly the oppression olympics, lets compare and contrast warrior benefits to every other class in the game:

Can a warrior have the highest damage performance- Yes
Can a warrior heal themselves with spells? - No
Can a warrior heal others for a short time after death? - No
Can a warrior resurrect a fallen teammate? - No
Can a warrior resurrect themselves? - No
Can a warrior summon other teammates to the location? - No
Can a warrior make portals to teleport themselves or teammates? - No
Can a warrior shape-shift and fulfill every role in the game? - No
Can a warrior stealth at will or easily escape combat - No
Can a warrior AoE farm by making it rain icicle spears or fireballs from the sky? - No
Can a warrior banish or polymorph targets? - No
Can a warrior set traps for targets? - No
Can a warrior grant levitate or slow fall to themselves or others? - No
Can a warrior walk on water or grant underwater breathing? - No
Can a warrior turn into a cheetah or wolf for increased movement speed? - No
Can a warrior grant Aspect of the Pack or Cheetah for increased movement speed? - No
Can a warrior tame pets or summon demons to aide them in combat? - No
Can a warrior grant a variety of buffs to party or raid members? - No

So then what significant value does a warrior provide to a party, you ask? The answer is damage. High freaking damage. And yet people hate on the warrior class for shining in the one single area that it excels at, despite it lacking in virtually every other aspect of class benefit comparatively. With that being considered, if every class were to be equal to warriors in terms of damage, then wtf would be the incentive to play a warrior over any other class?

P.S. Don't even try the "Warriors are the best tanks" argument. Warriors WERE the "best" tanks because vanilla WoW was released half-baked due to the time constraints of its development cycle. It wasn't intended for them to be the only viable tank class. TWoW has since rectified that issue with the Class Changes 2 patch. So all tanks are now viable and each uniquely excel in areas that are specific to their class.
Dude warrior is the best tank in the game. No reason for it, being a hybrid to also be the best dps in the game. It should have around the same dps as a smite priest imo.
You must be living under a rock because warrior is currently the worst tank of the game. You're actually gimping your raid to even bring one unless they are an outstanding tank. Druids and paladins are the meta now.

author: Abiozan
subject: Re: Warrior Envy is Nonsensical [Rant]
content_md:
I think the core issue people don't get with warrior is that warrior is the most useless class outside of a raid/group environment. They definitely tried changing it up a little by giving warrior stuff like blood drinker in fury (as well as blood craze being a must take now in fury), but even then for farming you definitely don't use a warrior, for raiding warrior tank is legit only better than memes like shaman tank, but the issue is not that warrior tank is now "bad", its just that the other specs are superior.

The reason why people bring tank warriors in "hardcore speedrunning guilds" is... Because they have a geared bis character who's a good player, and regearing a new character takes a while in classic, as well as some people just don't want to lvl new characters and you probably won't bench your core members because their class suddenly got nerfed to the ground.

DPS warrior is another thing, I mean sure it has the highest dps potential in the game, but warrior dps is already quite nerfed with no wbuffs (which is like a 20-40% dps increase alone), but on top of it warrior was arguably the most skill driven spec in an already kind of easy vanilla setting, and new warrior while doing dps is just kind of... lame now. You used to time cooldowns, now you just kinda slap them on as soon as debuffs are up/enrage procs.
And even if its the defacto best dps class, if you nerf its dps then realistically you just have no reason to bring warriors in a raid except like 5 for sunders and that's it.
I'm just surprised devs didn't give paladin/bear a sunder to truly rule out warriors from the meta. lmao.

edit: the problem with bringing sunder bot warriors is now you just have yet another "slave class" issue, and the current top dps non-slave classes would be hunter and arcane mages (maybe frost, but arcane is at least playable without respecs).
Blizzard may be questionable, but if warrior was designed this way, it was designed this way for a good reason. People thought it was legit underpowered before until people figured out how to get good.

author: Feetlover444
subject: Arms Warriors in need of more utility!
content_md:
Currently as of latest patch and every patch before that warriors got clowned on by literally every other class.

There's no matchup a warrior is strong against, literally none especially with latest patch, any class can easily dispatch a warrior.

The dps of a warrior is fine its not super amazing or anything but due to being a plate class I'm going to give it a pass.

But what a warrior severely lacks is being able to counterplay against all the other classes.

Wotlk gave us shattering throw to counter ice block/bubble.
TBC gave us spell reflect to counter all kinds of spells to which we are super weak against.
We also got second wind in TBC that helped us with sustain (A warrior should have good sustain due to not having any heal on demand in his kit)

Normally being a plate class you'd think you'd be the longest standing throughout a fight, but spells of course bypass any and all your armor and just disable you in 2 seconds either way with the burst heavy meta in pvp.

It makes no sense that a warrior can't hold his ground against any other class in a 1v1 situation, arms is severely lacking in utility being a PVP class foremost it needs more utility in its arsenal.

My proposal is having a good look at tbc warriors and perhaps bring some of that tbc utility to twow warriors. If you guys ever end up releasing rated arena's warriors in their current state won't be able to compete at all, it'll just be insane ccfest all over the place.

Another proposal I have is nerfing polymorphs stuns saps and fears, super long cc's are broken especially in the burst heavy meta we have. Make all of them have diminishing returns and maybe increase their cd's and slash their cc durations.

Tbh at current patch every other class or needs massive tuning down, or warriors just flatout need more utility in their kit to keep up with these overtuned classes.

author: Bigsmerf
subject: Re: Arms Warriors in need of more utility!
content_md:
Nah

There was a time in life where I'd been completely convinced warriors were dogshit in PvP, but I think it's safe to say the whole "Warrior is great with a healer!" take isn't as half baked as me and like two other people at best thought.

Think of it like this.

A warrior at max rage is dangerous. Big damage and mortal strike debuff can be pretty debilitating.

A warrior who can't be stopped is also dangerous. Faps are key in a lot of fights and having support from a paladin to remove CCs can be huge. Pally freedom is niche and not going to be readily available especially for the hordies (No fweedom, orc sadge) but ANYONE and everyone can use fap. Warrior just benefits from it more since it allows them to play their class better and crush face without being slowed/rooted. It covers their biggest weakness in the form of being kited.

These two factors can be achieved through one thing. Sustainability. If your warrior is getting heals, and they know how to play (free CC-begone button not required to do that surprisingly enough) they can be the sole cause for a close win in a team engagement. Want an important target debilitated and made easier to kill? Chase that healer (don't forget your fap) and mortal strike them. Keeping topped off will be infinitely more difficult and if you manage to hamstring or someone has them CC'd it'll make getting away more difficult, ultimately securing a kill.

Also- rogues. Rogue is warrior's one particular 1v1 "counter". This isn't to say a warrior will dominate a rogue, but they're definitely pretty advantaged in comparison to matchups with other classes. I will admit warriors are pretty mid in terms of duels and in the wild PvP encounters, but vanilla isn't meant to balance every class to be good in every niche. That just wouldn't be smart. Warrior is already the best DPS class. Apparently they're not the best tanks anymore but even besides that the fact that they're the de-facto best at anything proves there's some semblance of balance. And again, team fights. Warr fills a niche in BG PvP with the purpose of being a spearhead and enabler. If that warrior isn't getting clowned on then chances are someone would snap their focus right on the poor troll hunter who just wanted to spam steady shot and fight the evil alliance paladins.

For reference, none of this is me saying warrior is "OP" or already super busted- their kit isn't particularly potent by itself. What *is* busted though, is consumables, and strength in numbers. Warrior truly shines when they're enabled and given support. They have a niche, and require coordination. Imagine if arcane mages or pre-CC2 ele shams needed to pop a consume before they raw casted a fuckload of burst onto someone, or if paladins needed someone else to cast their bubble for them. These are exaggerations, of course, but the basic concept is the same. Warrior is bad. They need help. But not changes.

author: Abiozan
subject: Re: Arms Warriors in need of more utility!
content_md:
Warrior's pvp state is really weird, honestly.
At one hand warrior has a lot of potential being able to chase targets, apply a healing debuff and slow people as well as aoe fear people (every 3 minutes but still) + arguably best aoe burst in game, mage's good too but you don't get to do super big aoe in bgs minus for AV/WSG chokes and warrior cleaves best in smaller groups of people.

But the problem is warrior is like the definition of potential man. You can IF you get support, IF you get consumes, IF and WHEN you can be useful to a fight cuz you MIGHT do something. But it almost never is. The most game turning thing I ever did on a warrior was line up a sweeping strikes and a recklessness - a 30 minute CD, to actually do a push in AV.

Other classes can do much more in BGs and honestly even 1v1 scenarios by just.. existing, no consumes, no engi needed really either though grenades and some of the pvp trinkets + rocket helm are useful.

And that raises the question, why support, pocket and heal a class in BGs that has p o t e n t i a l to be good and pop off when you can heal literally anything else that already performs well by itself and be sure that it'll work.

Also I really do feel people really overestimate warrior's PVP damage output, unless you reck be ready to see like 450-500 mortal strike/auto attack crits on holy paladins and resto shamans, and keep in mind you have to like actually get into melee range and stay on the person to even do your job.

Something like second wind would be the best way to improve warrior's 1v1 ability but not make them OP unstoppable in groups.

The primary way(s) warriors benefit in groups are from heals and from the granting of mobility (i.e. blessing of freedom, dispels, FAPs, insignia trinket etc).  So adding a passive that grants health regen & rage ONLY when immobilized would really only be beneficial to a warrior when he is 1v1 or playing with a team that isn't being supportive.  If the immobilization is removed/ends, then the regen effect should end as well.

Makes a lot of sense to at least generate rage when immobilized because naturally this would be infuriating as a warrior.

This will never happen, but I feel like rage generation should be reversed in theory.  When you miss, get parried or dodged, don't crit, get rooted/slowed - these are the most "rage-inducing" moments as a warrior player; so it would be understandable to boost rage for the warrior in those moments - but when you get a big critical strike, it feels good - basically like a releasing of rage.  But I digress.

There's no matchup a warrior is strong against, literally none especially with latest patch, any class can easily dispatch a warrior.

The dps of a warrior is fine its not super amazing or anything but due to being a plate class I'm going to give it a pass.

But what a warrior severely lacks is being able to counterplay against all the other classes.

Wotlk gave us shattering throw to counter ice block/bubble.
TBC gave us spell reflect to counter all kinds of spells to which we are super weak against.
We also got second wind in TBC that helped us with sustain (A warrior should have good sustain due to not having any heal on demand in his kit)

Normally being a plate class you'd think you'd be the longest standing throughout a fight, but spells of course bypass any and all your armor and just disable you in 2 seconds either way with the burst heavy meta in pvp.

It makes no sense that a warrior can't hold his ground against any other class in a 1v1 situation, arms is severely lacking in utility being a PVP class foremost it needs more utility in its arsenal.

My proposal is having a good look at tbc warriors and perhaps bring some of that tbc utility to twow warriors. If you guys ever end up releasing rated arena's warriors in their current state won't be able to compete at all, it'll just be insane ccfest all over the place.

Another proposal I have is nerfing polymorphs stuns saps and fears, super long cc's are broken especially in the burst heavy meta we have. Make all of them have diminishing returns and maybe increase their cd's and slash their cc durations.


Tbh at current patch every other class or needs massive tuning down, or warriors just flatout need more utility in their kit to keep up with these overtuned classes.

There's no matchup a warrior is strong against, literally none especially with latest patch, any class can easily dispatch a warrior.

The dps of a warrior is fine its not super amazing or anything but due to being a plate class I'm going to give it a pass.

But what a warrior severely lacks is being able to counterplay against all the other classes.

Wotlk gave us shattering throw to counter ice block/bubble.
TBC gave us spell reflect to counter all kinds of spells to which we are super weak against.
We also got second wind in TBC that helped us with sustain (A warrior should have good sustain due to not having any heal on demand in his kit)

Normally being a plate class you'd think you'd be the longest standing throughout a fight, but spells of course bypass any and all your armor and just disable you in 2 seconds either way with the burst heavy meta in pvp.

It makes no sense that a warrior can't hold his ground against any other class in a 1v1 situation, arms is severely lacking in utility being a PVP class foremost it needs more utility in its arsenal.

My proposal is having a good look at tbc warriors and perhaps bring some of that tbc utility to twow warriors. If you guys ever end up releasing rated arena's warriors in their current state won't be able to compete at all, it'll just be insane ccfest all over the place.

Another proposal I have is nerfing polymorphs stuns saps and fears, super long cc's are broken especially in the burst heavy meta we have. Make all of them have diminishing returns and maybe increase their cd's and slash their cc durations.


Tbh at current patch every other class or needs massive tuning down, or warriors just flatout need more utility in their kit to keep up with these overtuned classes.
Did you wanted to play classic warrior for sure? Play something else.
Don't worry champ I've already quit and moved on to a different server where warriors are in a much better place, twow warriors suck fucking balls lmao.

author: rubixluffy
subject: Re: New AP scaling ratios? Concussion Blow description?
content_md:
Have the same question. Tests are confusing.

Damage of "Concussion Blow" is confusing.
Based on 5 points of talents "One-handed Weapon Specialization", we deal 110% damage in Battle Stance and 99% damage in Protection Stance.
Consussion Blow's base damage is 235.

Tests in Battle Stance:
AP | Damage | Extra AP Damage upon 100%Base | Extra AP Damage upon 110%Base
 410 | 296 | (296 - 235)/110% = 55 | 296/110% - 235 = 34
 648 | 332 | (332 - 235)/110% = 88 | 332/110% - 235 = 67
 802 | 355 | (355 - 235)/110% = 109 | 355/110% - 235 = 88
 1094 | 399 | (399 - 235)/110% = 149 | 399/110% - 235 = 128
Data of the 4th column(Extra AP Damage upon 110%Base) does not make sense.
So, based on the tested data, the 3rd column(Extra AP Damage upon 100%base) make sense.
That means "One-handed Weapon Specialization" does not affect Concussion Blow's base 235 damage.
In Battle Stance, damage of Concussion Blow = 235 + (AP/14 * 1.9).

Tests in Protection Stance:
AP | Damage | Extra AP Damage upon 100%Base | Extra AP Damage upon 99%Base
 410 | 266 | (266 - 235)/99% = 31 | 266/99% - 235 = 34
 648 | 298 | (298 - 235)/99% = 63 | 298/99% - 235 = 66
 802 | 319 | (319 - 235)/99% = 85 | 319/99% - 235 = 87
 1094 | 359 | (359 - 235)/99% = 125 | 359/99% - 235 = 128
Data of the 3rd column does not make sense. The 4th column's data are closed to Battle Stance's 4th column.
So, "One-handed Weapon Specialization" does affect Concussion Blow's base 235 damage.
But, how does AP affect damage? 410AP increase 34 damage, but 238AP(from 410 to 648) increase 32(from 34 to 66) damage.

I think that parry and tactical mastery both can belong to 1st row of talents.
You don't always want 5/5 tactical mastery, but if you want additional parry, you have to spend those points anyway. author: Turbosaxophonic
subject: Re: Prot tank talent tree, parry is misplaced.
content_md:
With that reasoning Prot should also be getting Fury’s Shout bonuses and recovery from being critically hit since that would benefit tanks as well. Warrior’s a tank/DPS hybrid and their talents should show that.

Each tree gets defensive options so Prot gets to keep building a tank in other trees after 40, but they’re also there to make early game tanking smoother if you aren’t specced Prot. Warrior as a whole is supposed to do well at defense even if they don’t specialize to tank, it’s important for each tree to have their own flavor of damage mitigation. In the case of Arms with its balance of offense and defense, they get Parry for their mastery of weapon technique since you can only block with a shield, this contrasts with Fury’s “bring it on” attitude to taking damage. Warriors are supposed to be able to stand toe-to-toe with their enemies in each spec.

I really hope this isn’t something that happens, CC2 moving Slam and its talent to Arms because “it’s the 2h spec” diluted the intended mechanical crossover with these trees and I don’t want to see more steps in that direction. I think it’s better when the talents don’t push you to build in one direction so much.

author: Berettadin
subject: Re: Can you share with me a pve warrior guide for turtle wow?
content_md:
My basic advice for leveling is choose Fury. The most important talents are about longevity and reducing downtime, and that means Blood Craze. You're getting critted every fight; 6% back makes a real difference.

Basics are Cruelty 5/5, Dual Wield Specialization 5/5, Blood Craze 3/3, Improved Shouts 5/5, (Demoralizing Shout is a staple and you're reducing damage taken), and Enrage 5/5. After that comes things better for your role as dps on in a team like Reckless Execute and Death Wish (or PvP with Battlefield Mobility), but for PvE leveling Flurry is excellent.

On the Arms side Improved Heroic Strike helps since HS is your primary rage spender. Improved Rend is a talent tax for later abilities -Rend itself is okay because it's cheap and can be used all the time but it's obnoxiously weak and not worth buffing. Tactical Mastery is only worth 1 thing: having enough Rage for Disarm. Improved Charge is ok, but it won't always work and DW's Rage gains even out not having it. Improved Overpower is actually quite nice since you'll generate a lot of enemy Dodges but it's not cheap.

Opening is Rend, Demoralizing Shout, Sunder Armor, and HS when you can afford it. You'll get a feel for what to do when. There's not a lot of complexity 'til endgame and besides forgetting to Hamstring things that run off and come back with friends there's not a lot to go wrong.

Professions: First Aid and Cooking are absolutely essential. To reiterate for emphasis downtime and survival are your weaknesses and you are the weakest class in game for buffs. Take the time to level Cooking.

Beyond that I like Alchemy and Herbalism since being able to heal and buff yourself is crucial. Late game this will mean things like Flasks and making money selling Mongoose Potions. Alternatively do whatever; anything except Enchanting is worth your time.

Finally Warrior is an expensive class. Heavier armor costs more to repair. You have more weapon skills to train then anyone. You are also more gear dependent so you will grind for upgrades more and spend more money. Late game this will be actually good as when you are finally fully upgraded you'll be the best or near-best tank or dps there is. It's just a loooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooong
journey. If by chance you make friends with a Priest to level with you'll both fly upwards with how much you compliment each other.

The rest is persistence. Good luck.

author: Captain4k
subject: [Defensive Tactics] Talent Criticism
content_md:
> Defensive Tactics: While wearing a shield, you retain 180% of the increased threat generation from Defensive Stance in other stances.
>  <Developer Comment> The point of this talent is to allow tanks wearing shields to sacrifice mitigation for more threat by swapping in and out of Defensive Stance. With this buff to this talent, players should experience noticeably higher threat done, outside than inside Defensive Stance.

Am I the only one that thinks [Defensive Tactics] is conceptually flawed? Why do we have a talent in the deep protection tree that is incentivizing tanks to *leave* defensive stance? How does a talent that adds viability to other stances appeal to a sword and board playstyle? Wouldn't it make more sense to give warriors increased threat viability inside of defensive stance, as opposed to using the stance as a lesser version of Shield Wall? Buffing the [Improved Thunder Clap] talent by allowing it to hit more targets (up to 6 targets) and having the base ability scale with AP would have been a simpler solution to help warrior AoE threat. [Defensive Tactics] seems like a poorly thought out talent that should have been heavily revised before release, in my opinion. I think the talent either needs to be reworked or replaced entirely. In it's current state it's effectively just a waste of a talent tree slot.

Are there any seasoned warrior tanks that can explain how to accurately utilize [Defensive Tactics]? If I'm misunderstanding the usefulness of the talent then feel free to inform me.

author: Ellifta
subject: Re: [Defensive Tactics] Talent Criticism
content_md:
It's a very good talent that gives every warrior basically a reason to use any stance while tanking. In short summary, here are what each stance does if you invest 3 points into defensive tactics and 5 points in defiance. Battle stance is very similar to using deathwish or using dual wield from old fury/prot tanking in the sense that it gives you more threat but less mitigation.

Battle Stance:
+7-8% more threat gained per point of damage dealt compared to defensive stance, 10% more damage compared to defensive stance, which roughly ends up to 15-20% more threat overall
Ability to use overpower and execute, especially good if you use impale/prot spec.
No crit or crush immunity because you don't have shield block, 10% more damage taken compared to defensive stance.

This stance is good when you want to maximize threat, such as Vaelstratz or Maexna. Very satisfying to play with overpower, but because you only get 1 shield block every 4.5 seconds you are open to crits and crushing blows. With 370 defence in Naxx, in my experience this leads to 1 crit per boss fight and usually 4-5 crushing blows.

Defensive Stance:
The classic stance, crit and crush immunity if using shield block and shield slam on CD and 10% less damage taken. Good for bosses that deal a lot of damage and you want to give up some threat for mitigation like twin emps, Chromaggus or Patchwerk.

Berserker Stance: 3% more crit, 10% more damage taken but access to Whirlwind for AoE threat and fear immunity.

This talent is an excellent way to choose between more mitigation or more threat for deep prot tank without having them dual wield. You always stick to your shield.

The core issue with ***[Defensive Tactics]*** isn't just numbers — it's conceptual. A Protection warrior should never have to abandon Defensive Stance to do their job. If a tank is forced to step into a more offensive stance just to hold aggro, something fundamental is broken.

The solution isn't to reward stance-dancing — it's to empower Protection's core identity: a resilient, shield-bearing wall that controls threat while mitigating damage.

Instead of encouraging tanks to leave their defensive tools behind, the tree should enhance and expand them.

Here are some concrete suggestions for improving [Defensive Tactics], or replacing it entirely:

![📌](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f4cc.svg) Add a new deep Protection talent (e.g., Improved Defensive Stance) that increases single-target threat by 30% while in Defensive Stance.

![📌](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f4cc.svg) Let Defense Skill scale with threat generation — rewarding gearing and proper progression.

![📌](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f4cc.svg) Introduce a new ability: Opportunity Attacks
When the warrior loses aggro, they immediately perform a low-damage retaliatory strike that immobilizes the target for 1 second and generates massive threat. This would be a flavorful, thematic mechanic inspired by Pathfinder and D&D 3.5e — rewarding positioning, awareness, and proper timing.

These kinds of changes would reinforce the true fantasy of a tank: holding the line, controlling the enemy, and protecting the raid — not dancing between stances or pretending to be Fury with a shield.

A deep Protection talent should feel essential, not optional or awkward to justify.
Let's bring real power back to sword and board.

Druids are "dodge tanks"
Paladins are "block tanks"

Deep prot 1/1

Druids are "dodge tanks"

Deep prot 1/1

Mid tree, tied to one of the revenge talents 3/3:

After using revenge your chance to parry is increased by 3/6/10% for 8 seconds or until you parry an attack.

author: Taralej90
subject: Re: [Defensive Tactics] Talent Criticism
content_md:
While leveling my HC warr, I've been looking at this talent in every way I can, with my 20 years of WoW experience, a lot of it with warrior. These are my conclusions:

 - In Battle Stance, you can use Overpower and Execute. The problem is Overpower is proc-based and therefore unreliable. Also, the value of Improved Overpower and Deep Wounds is very low if you're using a fast weapon. Furthermore, even if you were to stance-dance for Overpower procs, this means you're burning rage that you could've just used to queue up a Heroic Strike. Being able to use Execute while maintaining high threat is nice, but at that point of the fight threat is not an issue anyway. Healer mana is.
 - In Berserker Stance, you can use Whirlwind, Berserker Rage and, again, Execute. Whirlwind for AoE threat is OK, although far from ideal, especially if you're using a fast one-hander. Stance-dancing for Berserker Rage is something good tanks already know how to do, so the value here is actually pretty low.

In summary, using Defensive Tactics and sitting permanently in Battle Stance results in a gameplay that's very similar to vanilla Arms, swapping Mortal Strike for Shield Slam. You use Sunder Armor as a filler and lose access to Revenge, which also deals more threat than SA (similar with Defensive Tactics in Battle Stance) and is far more rage-efficient. You lose flat 10% mitigation and Shield Block for more threat. It is worth noting that, without a doubt, opening with Concussion Blow + Shield Slam would result in significantly more threat with Defensive Tactics and outside of Defensive Stance.

All in all, it's a cool talent, but I don't want to lose 10% mitigation for more threat. Move it up in order for it to be accessible by other builds and instead change One-Handed Weapon Specialization to Sword and Board, with the talent text reading: "Increases all damage you deal when a shield is equipped by 2/4/6/8/10%. Also increases the threat generated by Thunder Clap by XYZ". This would make the talent actually affect more than just your autos and would make it equal to Prot Pala's equivalent. I don't know why we're talking so much about Prot while ignoring the elephant in the room - this talent, situated very deep in the Prot tree, only affects our auto-attacks (and HS) and ignores Shield Slam and Revenge.

author: Eyeburn
subject: Re: [Defensive Tactics] Talent Criticism
content_md:
> **Xudo wrote: Sat Aug 16, 2025 3:49 pm**
> Actually, no. Vanilla tanking was built around stance dancing. Turtle reduced need to switch stances dramatically.

Not really.  The most stance dancing happened in dungeon pulls with charge engages.  Stance dancing for berserker rage doesn't take any real skill.  If anything, vanilla most harshly punished moving through stances or trying to use cross stance abilities.

The problem with Defensive Tactics is that it's a pseudo Warbringer talent while being obtuse to use.  It doesn't incentivize stance dancing because you're going to lose up to 75 rage every time you change a stance, so it's really opening avenues to tank in battle or berserker stance.  When you break down the benefits and drawbacks of either stance, all that's really being accomplished is tanking in battle stance so that Execute can be spammed at the end of the fight.  At the end of a fight is when you can swap to battle stance even without this talent and hit execute without any real possibility of losing threat.

If the idea is to open up which abilities a prot warrior can use, just put Warbringer as a replacement.  If the idea is that tank warriors need to retain threat generation to spam execute safely, then this talent is wildly missing the mark.

author: Gladius
subject: Hamstring nerf was unnecessary and is a huge deal
content_md:
Me, another warrior and a druid were farming Zul'Mamwe troll ruins in STV. Another druid 3-4 levels lower than us harassed the shit out of us with moonfire and range. Would hit us when we were fighting troll and panther packs.

Shapeshifted right out of our hamstrings the 3 or 4 times he made a mistake and came in our Intercept range. Managed to escape every time. Only once did he need to use a grenade (probably an engineer).

Why does warrior's hamstring have a CD when druid's shapeshift does not?! That does not make sense. I understand that warriors have high damage but warriors in pvp 1v1 are not overpowered. Just do a flat out 10% or even 20% damage reduction if you want to but do not take away the small amount of mobility that warriors have.

Today I got camped by a hunter. I managed to kill him twice when he made a lot of mistakes (out of 8 times) but 30 seconds CD on intercept (which hunter's shots can also outrange) and Turtle wow's addition of 6 second CD on hamstring is absolutely insane and damning.

I'm not complaining on execute nerf. Just give us hamstring back. Some kind of real mobility (not the RNG Counterattack).

Also, warrior is not popular because of the purported reason that he is OP. Warrior is popular because its the only non-magical honorable (vs rogue) melee in classic. And has fun mechanics/rotation. Nerf the damage output if you are so concerned about warriors being OP. Dont nerf the mechanics and especially mobility mechanics please.

subject: Re: Hamstring nerf was unnecessary and is a huge deal
content_md:
Nerf affects every area.

Leveling.

PvP.

PvE to an extent as well.

In essence, you have no Improved Hamstring - - Counterattack sucks, is costlier, shorter, and has fewer possible cases of use.

Sword Specialization can hardly be fished for.

Hand of Justice, anything else like it, and Windfury Totem fishing remain the same through Sunder instead, but it is damageless amongst other factors - - on top of not being able to fish for Crits to proc Deep Wounds and, more relatably here due to changes, certain new effects if you have them (Set Bonuses).

Everyone whosoever argues that it was deserved or that it's no big deal is merely baiting or missing every manner of clues as to just how important these blatant nerfs are, and ought to roll a Warrior, level without being boosted, do endgame PvE, and especially PvP - - otherwise, just shut up and complain about your Hybrid Class not having enough buffs.

author: Eyeburn
subject: Re: Hamstring nerf was unnecessary and is a huge deal
content_md:
Most private projects over nerf warriors on the basis that they were really strong with the world buff meta on other servers and in classic WoW in 2019.  Yeah, that much is true, warrior dps scaled the hardest with world buffs, and warrior tanks were the only real tanking options for raid by design.  Those flaws were real.

Addressing those issues goes beyond just picking away at the warrior's toolkit.  Can you stop wf fishing by slapping a big CD on hamstring?  Yes.  Is it the best way to stop wf fishing?  No.  If anything adding the CD slows down the fishing, but it will still be used to fish for a proc, but now warriors are also significantly nerfed in PvP.

People may say that warriors were OP in PvP, but these people are wrong and never played through the ranking meta.  Premade honor grinding stomp groups weren't warrior stacked, they were engineer stacked because sappers mattered more than anything else.  After that it you wanted a couple warriors for frontline engagement, and you always wanted a druid.  Vanilla bg meta groups are surprisingly well balanced in terms of class representation for the best results.

The real solution to wf fishing is removing hamstring's ability to proc it, not slapping a significant CD onto hamstring.

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: Arms warrior DPS rotation
content_md:
You should be in Berserker Stance all the time to benefit from the extra Crit in spite of the additional Damage intake, as Battle Stance offers nothing and Defensive Stance instead lowers your output.

Overpower is also only available if ever your opponent performs a Dodge on any of your attacks - - else, it is unusable.

You should be using Whirlwind off Cooldown and having Slam be your filler whenever both MS and WW are unavailable, you have no Overpower to use, and there is nothing to Execute.

Furthermore, you should Slam relatively the same as you would in original Vanilla; sure, the Swing Timer here continues rather than pause (post-Vanilla) or reset (Vanilla), but the increased Cast Time of 2.5s (untalented) or 2s (Improved Slam 2/2) means that you will almost always have to use it just about immediately upon swinging. You may have enough time for one Ability (1 GCD, 1.5s wait time), but that may vary a lot and takes a lot of discipline to keep consistent.

You should also consider using Hamstring as an instant filler, despite its atrocious custom 6s CD, because it can still be used as a means of fishing for procs for Sword Specialization, Hand of Justice, and Windfury Totem, as well as whatever other chance-based effects you may have on top of all of that combined. Personally, I run without Improved Slam, and generally don't use Slam itself all that much, instead cycling MS/WW and fishing with Hamstring or stacking/refreshing Sunder, then using something else like Cleave (if AoE), and that is after initially activating Sweeping Strikes at the start (also if AoE), so I usually do not have downtime, and even if I do, it's better to just wait a short while to swing normally and get back to the rotation.

You should only ever really bother with Heroic Strike as a last-resort Rage dump if you have nothing available and your Rage is at 70 or more; implying 15R (untalented) as well as not producing Rage from your next swing, followed by MS and then WW - - that should spend all your Rage (implying no OP proc or Execute phase, no swing procs to immediately generate extra Rage).

Of course, this is how I've learnt to do it, and it has worked quite well for me; others may do it differently to their own benefit.

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: Arms warrior DPS rotation
content_md:
Note that for ordinary enemies (standard Mobs and weak Elites that die quickly), you should consider using Sunder only up to 50% remaining Health.

Additionally, Sunder Armor can still be used to proc certain effects, but not nearly as many as using Hamstring can: it can for example proc the Crusader Weapon Enchantment, but will not trigger Sword Specialization as an Arms Warrior.

The effectiveness of Sunder Armor's Debuff depends on how much Armor the Target has to begin with: if it has a lot, the benefit won't be big, as there will still be a lot of leftover Armor, but some is better than a lot more (especially with more Damage Dealers with you who rely on Physical Damage as their main source); if, however, the Armor is little as it is, the returns are larger, and by removing that amount, you end up restoring more of the otherwise-reduced Physical Damage you'd be dealing to the same enemy. You must however exercize caution with exceptionally low-armored enemies (not Bosses but other Mobs, and some Player Classes), as you cannot reduce Armor below 0 -- attempting to stack Sunder more than you would need would only be a waste.

Still better than using Rend starting from about Level 20, though, so indeed, use it more frequently and train yourself to know when and how to best use it, depending on the scenario in front of you.

subject: Re: Arms warrior DPS rotation
content_md:
Yes, and you should prefer to use your biggest Cooldowns during that period (Human Racial for extra Crit OR Recklessness; Bloodrage if you're running Enrage but that's unlikely to have in PvE), and time the Executes so that you're getting the most out of the Rage that you use up -- swing and then use Execute, since you might get a Crit for fat Rage (plus a Sword Spec which could be its own Crit), likely capping you out, allowing a max-burst Execute, then Precision Cut will give back tons, and then either do it again (especially if Execute procs Hand of Justice or Windfury Totem or Sword Spec for more Rage right back again), or wait for another swing and then Execute again.

Get a good rhythm and become comfortable with adapting it dynamically, and you should see some good numbers.

author: Davdes1
subject: Warrior T3.5/Kara40 problem
content_md:
almost every class has a variation of their T3.5/Kara40 set according to which role they play, whether tank heal or dps. For instance, the paladin, shaman and druid each have 3 separate version of this set according to which spec they play. But freaking warrior has only one for 2 roles they can play. Their actual set is a mix of dps and tank.

The T2.5 had the same problem with diluted power since it shared dps + tank stats. Please don't repeat the same mistake as the T2.5, make one version of the set which is for Arms/Fury and one for Protection.

Follow the example of Tier 4, Blizzard had fixed this matter with the Tier 4 in TBC for warriors. (Warbringer Battlegear (Arms/Fury) or Warbringer Armor (Protection)

Please do the same. One Tier 3.5/Kara40 warrior set version for Arms/Fury and one for Protection. You gave paladin, shaman and druid 3 versions each. At least give warrior 2 versions, they also have the right since they got 2 roles/functions!

''Paladins... 3 different roles; tank, heal and dps: earn 3 versions of their set (whoaaa!).''
''Mages... 1 role; dps: earn 2 versions of their set (Yeahhh!)
''Warriors... **2 different roles; tank and dps: earn 1 version of their set** (Doh!).''

author: Manletow
subject: Warrior is Inherently Bad (in PVP)
content_md:
The Warrior class is fundamentally doomed to failure in general PVP scenarios.

The reasons are countless but i'll give a couple examples:

First of all -- Rage is balanced around PVE content.

Dumbass NPC mobs hit the Warrior with generic melee attacks allowing him to get rage without dying too fast -- as a healer tops off the Warriors HP.

Competent players will just ignore/CC a Warrior -- cucking them of Rage -- and clapping said Healer instead.

Important Note:
Every single class starts a fight (respawn from GY) at their most powerful -- with full resources available (AKA Mana/Energy).

Warrior is the sole exception -- they begin every fight at their absolute weakest and most useless: 0 Rage
Warrior is known for Charge ---> Graveyard (due to no survivability/escape tools) so they will be constantly in a state of pathetic impotence.

In PVE -- AKA Raid Boss Fights -- long slow paced battles are standard. Giving ample time to build rage.
In PVP -- battles are over in a matter of seconds. No time at all to gain Rage. Simply Die too fast.

Secondly -- Armor is balanced around PVE content.

 90% of NPC only attack using generic physical hits -- this makes Heavy Armor/Shield very useful and viable.
Warrior essentially has no defense/survivability in PVP because roughly 66% of Players are using Magic Damage only.

Conclusion:
Warrior will continue to be hopelessly inept and dead weight in PVP Battlegrounds (and WPVP) unless massive reworks (or additional tools/abilities) are implemented.

However -- Turtle WoW is specifically designed/intended to be conservative in nature.
The unfortunate result?

Warrior will NEVER be viable. It should simply not be played in PVP.
I'm sorry. I really am.   sad_turtle

author: Voodoochile
subject: Re: wep setup?
content_md:
The current answer is probably better rage generation still.

But in Vanilla and before CC2 (may it be damned) the reason why you would use an OH faster than your MH is that Heroic Strike uniquely bypassed the OH bonus inaccuracy while it was queued up. Meaning that having an OH that would consistently get swings between your MH swings got more value out of this Heroic Strike mechanic, which translated to more rage and more damage.

But they got rid of that mechanic because of.... reasons, surely.
content_html:
The current answer is probably better rage generation still.

author: Wilsonsds
subject: Suggestion: Improving Protection Warrior Threat Management
content_md:
Protection Warriors still struggle to keep up in threat generation, even after recent changes. While they lack strong AoE threat tools — and that's fine — they should at least excel in single-target threat, which is currently not the case.

---
 **![🛡️](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f6e1.svg) Key Suggestions:**

 **1. End-Tier Talent: Improved Defensive Stance**
Introduce a final-tier Protection talent that increases threat generation by **at least 30%** while in Defensive Stance.
This would give Prot Warriors a solid identity as single-target tanks and help them fulfill their intended role more reliably.

 **2. Make Defense Skill Contribute to Threat**
Tie **Defense rating** or skill directly to threat generation.
This would add depth to gearing choices and reward tanks who invest in defensive stats — both thematically and mechanically.

 **3. New Ability: Opportunity Attacks**
Inspired by Pathfinder and D&D 3.5e, this would be a reactive ability exclusive to Prot Warriors:

- Triggers an **automatic melee attack** when the warrior *loses threat* on a target
Deals *low damage*, but generates **high threat**
- **Immobilizes** the target for **1 second**
This would give Prot Warriors a unique, skill-based mechanic to recover threat in clutch moments, reinforcing their role as disciplined, control-oriented tanks.

---
These ideas aim to **enhance single-target threat generation** without making Prot Warriors overpowered in AoE or altering their core identity.
The class fantasy is strong — it just needs tools to stay competitive in modern encounters.

Protection warriors need single target threat. PERIOD. They do dumpster DPS, so at least allow them to maintain threat on a single target. This is the #1 issue with protection warrior. Ways to address this:

 1) Add a flat threat modifier to Improved Taunts (i.e. +500 flat threat and 1 second reduced cooldown) for each point

 2) Increase scaling for Shield Slam (i.e. increase AP scaling from 0.15 to 0.3)

 3) Add scaling for Revenge (i.e. add AP scaling of 0.15 for revenge)

 4) Add scaling for Concussion Blow (i.e. add AP scaling of 0.15 for revenge)

 5) Increase flat threat modifier for Concussion Blow (i.e. double the current flat modifier)

 6) Add a new talent 'Devastate' which adds AP scaling to Sunder Armor

Any or ALL of the above would be massive fixes to aid single threat target generation for protection warrior. None of these would make protection warriors better damage dealers than furyprot tanks or defensive tactics tanks, but they would allow protection tanks to be a non meme spec and do what protection warriors want to do (i.e. mitigate damage and mantain agro on a single target)

author: Zamera
subject: What is our identity in PvP
content_md:
Warriors at the moment are just glorified target dummies in PvP. We provide no useful utility, crowd control, and our damage is mediocre at best. We require multiple other specific classes/specs to perform at a baseline level. The upcoming patch addresses nothing, specifically for Arms PvP. I always saw Arms warrior as a tactical juggernaut, but none of this fantasy is felt in the game.

The upcoming patch provides a 10% buff to Mortal Strike and Slam, this is nerfed in instanced pvp combat and is really a win more buff. We will not really feel this. This is really a compensatory buff for PvE due to the execute changes.

Master Strike is very mediocre. While it is interesting to swap weapons in and out depending on the situation, not all weapons are created equal and acquiring multiple high end weapons seems like a tall tale to ask all warriors to do. Combine this with the rage cost and swapping weapons imposes a GCD penalty and resets your swing timer.

Some suggestions:

Unlink our big 3 cooldowns, Retaliation, Recklessness, and Shield Wall. It feels ancient that these are all the same cooldown still. Impose a 2 min cooldown when you activate one of them. Preferably I would like the big 3 cooldowns to be about 15 mins. Remove the Improved Disciplines talent from the game. It is border line useless with all the restrictions/other talents we can take.

Remove the shared cooldown on intervene and intercept.

Create a new spell, War Banner. Let this provide some sort of buff utility. Potentially we could see 3 of these for each spec/stance or we could limit it to one version. Let the banners be placeable and warriors can intervene them like an ally.

Arms Banner: Group movement speed increase, movement speed cannot go below x%, maybe reduces incoming crowd control (not CC that has already been applied)

Fury Banner: Some sort of group crit buff/crit dmg modifier increase?

Prot Banner: Mimics your health/armor, increases threat generation, pulses threat, if you cast taunt or maybe if you taunt it, it aoe taunts mobs onto it for 2s. Gives you the threat when it expires/dies.

Spell reflect or some sort of spell block.

Second Wind- health/rage when crowd controlled/immobilized

Victory Rush- medium damage- heals for 20% of max hp, resets on kill/hk (and assist) 20 sec cd

Holmgang- preventing most attacks from reducing your HP to less than 1. Duration: 10s chains a target to the warrior (stolen from ff14)

Nascent Flash- grants a high amount of vampirism for 10s (maybe like 50%) (stolen/similar to ff14)

Please note I am not asking for all this, these are suggestions in a way the game can go for Warriors (arms mainly).

Please comment on what you would like see/improve for Warriors or the direction you would like to see them go for us.

Combine this with the rage cost and swapping weapons imposes a GCD penalty and resets your swing timer.



Some suggestions:

Unlink our big 3 cooldowns, Retaliation, Recklessness, and Shield Wall. It feels ancient that these are all the same cooldown still. Impose a 2 min cooldown when you activate one of them. Preferably I would like the big 3 cooldowns to be about 15 mins. Remove the Improved Disciplines talent from the game. It is border line useless with all the restrictions/other talents we can take.

Remove the shared cooldown on intervene and intercept.

Create a new spell, War Banner. Let this provide some sort of buff utility. Potentially we could see 3 of these for each spec/stance or we could limit it to one version. Let the banners be placeable and warriors can intervene them like an ally.

Arms Banner: Group movement speed increase, movement speed cannot go below x%, maybe reduces incoming crowd control (not CC that has already been applied)

Fury Banner: Some sort of group crit buff/crit dmg modifier increase?

Prot Banner: Mimics your health/armor, increases threat generation, pulses threat, if you cast taunt or maybe if you taunt it, it aoe taunts mobs onto it for 2s. Gives you the threat when it expires/dies.

Spell reflect or some sort of spell block.

Second Wind- health/rage when crowd controlled/immobilized

Victory Rush- medium damage- heals for 20% of max hp, resets on kill/hk (and assist) 20 sec cd

Holmgang- preventing most attacks from reducing your HP to less than 1. Duration: 10s chains a target to the warrior (stolen from ff14)

Nascent Flash- grants a high amount of vampirism for 10s (maybe like 50%) (stolen/similar to ff14)


Please note I am not asking for all this, these are suggestions in a way the game can go for Warriors (arms mainly).

Please comment on what you would like see/improve for Warriors or the direction you would like to see them go for us.

content_md:
With the correct support, warriors demolish everything and the unique thing with Warriors is that they scale the best and have infinite amount of resources potentially. However, without dispels and healing, theyre easily controlled. But they're VERY gear dependent. As a healer, I LOVE sticking to geared Warriors since it's the most fun. But I can also imagine that being a PUG warrior can be extremely annoying if you don't have competent healers that are intent on keeping you alive.

 **Spell reflect:** We desperately need to incorporate more skill-based plays in this game and for Warriors I def think that it would be absolutely essential to give you guys spell reflect. This would def make casters think before they recklessly target warriors. Imagine the JOY of a mage polying themselves or pom pyroing themselves, rofl. I can see it.

 **Hamstring**: Remove the CD, it's ridiculous. If they keep it they need to be consistent, i.e. we need to see cooldowns on stuff like frostbolt aswell, which sounds stupid but so is the Hamstring CD.

 **Shattering throw**: Would provide great utility vs Palas and Mages.

However, I am also concious that giving Warriors more buffs other than these would make them extremely potent when getting supported too. So it's an interesting discussion to have. At the same time, we have classes like Warlocks that absolutely wreck 1n1 and they also do extremely well with support. I think that a removal of death coil would be ideal since that would also mean they would require more support and they wouldn't be able to wreck everyone 1n1. Imagine if Warriors got a ranged CC, that healed them and damaged the enemy hard?

author: Xudo
subject: Re: What is our identity in PvP
content_md:
I dunno about high levels, but level 19, warriors are kitable by almost all classes.
Paladins doesn't really care about hamstring and can successfully fight back. Fight get resolved by gear.
Hunters can send pet forward. If that doesn't work, then hunters almost simultaneously put scorpid sting/concussive shot, but even if warriors apply Hamstring, hunter can Wing Clip back and be faster than warrior.
Rogues can't kite warrior. Fight get resolved by gear.
Priests put warrior in combat with SWP before charge. Then warrior have to get through shield and Psychic Scream.
Shamans can kite around Earthbind totem. They can't put warrior in combat before charge, but earthbind totem provides better slow than Hamstring.
Mages just Frost nova after charge and can keep warrior slowed endlessly with rank 1 frostbolt.
Warlocks can put warrior in combat and then kite while warrior dying from Corruption/Agony and/or Imp.
Druids can fairie fire before charge and root while warriors is running. They can also get gap by Bash in Bear form or by Nature Grasp.

So basically, warrior job is to charge and be a threat that everyone should avoid in melee.
Super dumb role to be honest.

Yesterday I have seen warrior which did his job super good. He just stood afk in mid of WSG and enemy players spend mana to kill him. Meanwhile he was healed from other side. Then reinforcements arrived and killed attackers.

I personally given up on playing warrior on lvl 19 and made hunter.
Pummel and Slam at this bracket are good, but not enough to make a difference. Hunters for some reason got just instant melee attack without any cast time.

I dunno about high levels, but level 19, warriors are kitable by almost all classes.
Paladins doesn't really care about hamstring and can successfully fight back. Fight get resolved by gear.
Hunters can send pet forward. If that doesn't work, then hunters almost simultaneously put scorpid sting/concussive shot, but even if warriors apply Hamstring, hunter can Wing Clip back and be faster than warrior.
Rogues can't kite warrior. Fight get resolved by gear.
Priests put warrior in combat with SWP before charge. Then warrior have to get through shield and Psychic Scream.
Shamans can kite around Earthbind totem. They can't put warrior in combat before charge, but earthbind totem provides better slow than Hamstring.
Mages just Frost nova after charge and can keep warrior slowed endlessly with rank 1 frostbolt.
Warlocks can put warrior in combat and then kite while warrior dying from Corruption/Agony and/or Imp.
Druids can fairie fire before charge and root while warriors is running. They can also get gap by Bash in Bear form or by Nature Grasp.

So basically, warrior job is to charge and be a threat that everyone should avoid in melee.
Super dumb role to be honest.

Yesterday I have seen warrior which did his job super good. He just stood afk in mid of WSG and enemy players spend mana to kill him. Meanwhile he was healed from other side. Then reinforcements arrived and killed attackers.

I personally given up on playing warrior on lvl 19 and made hunter.
Pummel and Slam at this bracket are good, but not enough to make a difference. Hunters for some reason got just instant melee attack without any cast time.

In general though, I enjoyed melee classes (& the core mechanics) so much more back in my pre-WoW DAoC MMORPG days.

subject: Deep Wounds is only doing ~35% weapon damage instead of 60%
content_md:
Dragunovi wrote: 12 Oct 2024 18:31
Deep Wounds now deals damage every 1.5 seconds and lasts 6 seconds.
Developer Comment: This change makes Deep Wounds more useful even in situations where its quickly refreshed by multiple Warriors (such as raids), allowing it to deal atleast a part of its damage before its replaced while doubling its output for situations outside of raids.

author: Oomentaloo
subject: Re: Is Arms still the BIS Leveling Tank Spec
content_md:
You can tank with every spec. I like to take Tactical Mastery, so I can play around with all the tools of the warrior. The mobs don't hit hard enough so you don't get much out of Prot imho.
So if you are tanky enough for the dungeons you need threat and rage. you get threat and rage through damage and threat spells that cost rage. So as long your are not a too heavy burden on your healer dw or 2h tanking is good and maybe even easier.
But when the mobs are hitting too hard you have to have a shield to mitigate some dmg.
On Edwin Van Cleef or Verdan the Everliving in Wailing Caverns I would probably put on the shield, but trash mobs can mostly be tanked without.
TacMastery lets you do stuff like Charge -> Def stance -> ThunderClap -> Demo Shout.

So macros for weapon/shield swap and macro for shield block that has the shield swap built-in is a nice thing to have.

author: Snoof
subject: Re: Final Plea: Warrior in PVP
content_md:
"Useless" is being dramatic imo. Warrior is very good at a couple of things in PvP — pressuring healers, killing squishy melees and surprising mispositioned casters with high burst damage. The big problem with the class is just that it''s really, REALLY overreliant on things that aren't in its kit to function in PvP, be that consumables or the help of a support class.

Warriors are the only class that doesn't have any spammable general-purpose defensive abilities to use in PvP; that's by far the biggest issue if you ask me. The closest we get are retaliation/shield wall/recklessness and intimidating shout. The first option **is** super powerful in the right situation, but the cooldown is so long you only get to cast it once every other BG. Intimidating shout is also a pretty long cooldown, and as a fear it's some of the most unreliable CC in the game the way things are right now — especially if you're alliance going up against Will of the Forsaken and tremor totems. We struggle too much to pin targets down while being extremely easy to kite, and we die too quickly trying.

The other two big problems I see are shields and LiPs. Not being able to generate rage on shields is absolutely crippling, and it's complete nonsense to boot. I'm convinced it was never a deliberate balancing decision to begin with. imagine how stupid it would be if rogues stopped generating energy while hitting a shielded target, or ret paladins had to play the start of every fight against a shielded enemy without a mana bar; that's playing warrior when priests are around. I really can't overstate how much it sucks to deal with. LiPs meanwhile are just bullshit in general; whether you like the vanilla WoW brand of consumable spam pay-to-play PvP or not, I don't see how anybody could make a reasonable case for a potion that gives everybody a paladin bubble against phys damage classes being okay. There should either be an equivalent potion against magic damage, or they simply shouldn't exist in PvP.

My dream changes for warrior right off the bat would be:

 - Charge available in combat.
it's extremely easy for caster classes to cast some nothing spell like pain or counterspell at max range to get you in combat and deny you the ability to enter the fight with any kind of momentum in a way that feels much more like abusing a technicality than intelligent counterplay. And yes, I know that intercept exists; it costs rage that you don't have at the start of a fight and deprives you of all mobility for the rest of the encounter if used as an opener. You need both to have any hope of a mage even noticing you're there.

 - Slow immunity for the duration of Berserker Rage; Improved Berserker Rage moved to a more accessible place in the fury tree.
Warrior badly needs some kind of counterplay to CC built into its kit — Improved Berserker Rage is a good idea, but right now it's so deep in the PvE spec that the arms warriors that actually need it can't access it at all.

 - Homogenize Master Strike.
Master Strike is infinitely more useful than Counter Attack was, but it's still an extremely inconsistent ability. I'm sorry to say it, but trying to make an ability do that many different things is just not a good idea; the game's not deep enough to support it. What you've ended up with is the same exact thing as with Master of Arms: axes being the 'correct' option. Swords? Warriors already had disarm. Maces? Disorient's just worse CC for a class that auto-applies DoTs when it hits you. Polearms? Excessively niche, only useful against targets that **aren't** trying to fight you. Daggers, fists and staves? What even is the point? We don't get to use these weapons, and none of the effects are good enough that anybody's gonna bother carrying around extra weapons to use them. If they **were** that good they'd be OP. Trying to swap weapons situationally with primitive classic era macros completely sucks, and practically nobody bothers. Keep the root and scrap the rest.

 -Defensive Cooldown Rework.
Nerf the effects, dramatically shorten their cooldowns. Make shield wall usable without a shield (name change?)

 - Rage vs shields.

subject: Warrior Spell Changes & Talent Tree Changes
content_md:
"Every class has its bonus. If it's a Warrior complaining about a Mage, well guess what the Warrior is in the raid and the Mage isn't."

I decided to make a forum post to show some changes and talent trees I made for Warrior, because I want to see every Warrior spec do better in PvP in a way similar to WotLK Warrior. My reason is because the Classic+ goal of every class/spec dealing enough damage or being able to tank in the highest level raid content in Turtle WoW has been achieved. I think Warrior should now receive changes aimed towards being less miserable in PvP without an extreme amount of consumable usage and a pocket healer.

[https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... Vb&class=1](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t0=x1SNUNtNkf&t1=ETXHFzUP3T&t2=s1HwuVS2Vb&class=1)
Credit to Willwonka for several ideas from his talent tree

- **Shield Wall** will persist after unequipping a shield.

- **Recklessness**, **Shield Wall**, and **Retaliation** no longer share a cooldown with each other. Activating one of them will now put the other two spells on a two minute cooldown.

- **Hamstring** no longer has a cooldown, and can no longer grant **Flurry** or proc weapon effects.

- **Improved Overpower** now grants 25/50% critical strike damage bonus on Overpower instead of 25/50% critical strike chance.
New Spell: **Spell Reflection** (Rank 1)
Learned at Level 54
Raise your shield, reflecting the next spell cast on you.  Lasts 5 seconds.
Requires Battle Stance, Defensive Stance
Instant, 25 Rage, 10 second cooldown

author: Manletow
subject: Revamped Warrior Talent Trees (FINAL)
content_md:
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/H6PojEa.png)

My goals were to address deeply unfair/unfun PVP gameplay problems --
Whilst being as conservative as possible.
I also know T-WoW devs are highly adverse to TBC and WoTLK so I tried to avoid copy/pasting.
Special thanks to 'Kyrsie/Willwonka' for providing framework/inspiration.

 **BASELINE CHANGES:**
Charge now has a 1.5 second stun.
Intercept damage is based off Attack Power.
Revenge has a 45% chance to stun for 3 seconds.
Rend's Bleed Damage increased by 20%.
Hamstring snare duration is reduced to 12 seconds.

>>[**LINK TO NEW TALENT TREES**](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t0=Nb8LXgLHY3&t1=kM2pVBwMNI&t2=tai_ojUqFw)<<

 **[ARMS](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/tree/Nb8LXgLHY3) (Brief Notes):**
Given more control over enemies (lower CD Hamstring and chance to root).

(Conditionally) increased self-healing from Healing Potion...
and all other sources. Actually makes a Warrior a desirable healing target.

Sundering Strikes gives you a reason to wail on Tanks (commonly seen in T-WoW PVP).

Shattering Slam sometimes (requires luck) breaks an Immunity Shield (Bubble/Ice Block/LiP/etc)
(these are deeply problematic in PVP mostly cuz of having 0 direct counterplay options).

 **[FURY](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/tree/kM2pVBwMNI) (Brief Notes):**
They are already in a decent spot so I primarily gave them more flavor.
Specifically -- 'crazed maniac zoomie mobility'.

 **[PROT](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/tree/tai_ojUqFw) (Brief Notes):**
Bloodrage will allow a Warrior to gain Rage whilst beating on Immunity Shields and 'Absorb Shields' -- things such as PW: Shield, Ice Barrier, various trinkets, etc.
Increased support + mobility in one talent. (Speed boost for Warrior + partner)
More resist/survivability against all spells.
Can outright cockblock certain types of spells (Projectile).

author: Ellifta
subject: Re: How does the math of defensive tactics actually work?
content_md:
Defiance does count for other stances if you have defensive tactics talent, but the calculation is a bit confusing. Assuming you will always take 5/5 defiance as a warrior tank, the formula for default defensive stance threat is the following. Defiance is multiplicative, not additive.

t_dStanceDefiance = t_dStance × t_defiance
t_dStanceDefiance = 1,30 × 1,15 = 1,495

Per 1 point of damage, you do 1,495 point of threat in defensive stance normally. With defensive tactics talent 3/3 the following formula applies when calculating how much threat MULTIPLIER you have in other stances.

t_dTactics = (t_dStanceEffective - 1) × 1,8 + 1
Since you should be using Defiance at all times while tanking at max level we calculate:

t_dTactics = (1,495 - 1) × 1,8 + 1 = 1,891

 1,891 is not the final multiplier though, because there's a hidden 0.8 threat modifier in battle and berserker stance for warriors, just like rogues and feral druids do. In battle stance you do 10% more damage and get access to overpower and execute. In rough terms this will lead to 15% more threat compared to not having any defensive tactic talent points and staying in defensive stance.

author: Sylbrosa
subject: Warriors are too nerfed for PvP
content_md:
hi! Long time warrior player here.

I'm new to turtle wow and I'm really enjoing the experience, I just hit level 44 with my warrior and I'm having a lot of fun with the new zones, dungeons etc... So first of all, good job Turtle Team! You guys are nailing it!

So I love PvP. Personally I think it's wow's true late-game, and where it really shines. But I'm noticing that warriors have been nerfed a lot in Turtle WoW. And that's not a bad thing, they where too OP on classic wow. The thing is warriors have been nerfed out of existence?

I pick the meele class because I want to beat other players at meele, but then a shaman comes along and I die in 2 seconds??? I can deal with rogues alright. Some people are complaining about them but they are manageable. In comparison I've taken bursts of 2000 damage in less than 2 seconds from a Shaman. **And that's all my health**. Yes I've died in 2 seconds.

They walk up to you and just delete you.

And since they walk faster then us because wolf. You can't really get away...

I mean, it's gotten to a point where the battleground team with more shamans win? At least that's what I'm feeling whenever I enter a battleground. But of course shamans being broken is another topic, and I'm sure the Turtle Team knows this.

The thing is, warriors should be the strongest meele class. Shamans are casters, they shouldn't delete you up close, they should delete you at a distance. But if you get up and personal, that's warrior territory! You shouldn't get up and personal with a warrior!

I think the problem with shamans sums down to meele magical damage. My armor does nothing against magical damage. So when a shaman bursts me at meele, I just die.

This is how I feel whenever a shaman gets near me:

![Image](https://media.tenor.com/RBrUuN4z0ewAAAAe/guess-ill-die.png)

I think shamans need a nerf, make some of that magical damage into physical, or give the warrior a method to handle taking bursts of damage in pvp. That would be even cooler, and tie into the 'Master at Arms' talents about switching weapons! Maybe a shield talent for arms that allows you to block some incoming spells with shield block? That way the warrior still has to have the skill to switch to the shield, and go defensive mode until the shaman's mana gives up. And the shaman can keep his absurd deleting damage.

I have been having a blast with Master Strike. Like goddamn what a cool ability! I use it to root, dismount and disarm and I keep changing my weapon acording to what I need. Amazing idea! Just amazing!

PS: I noticed whirlwind is a level 36 ability, but improved whirlwind is a lvl 31 talent?

author: Ellifta
subject: Re: Warrior tier 2
content_md:
Warrior tank got the short end of the stick with CC2. Deep prot was buffed and was meant to be itemized around shield block value and crit, but none of the warrior tier sets have both of these stats in the same set. I'm not saying within the same item, I'm saying within the same entire tier set.

Fury prot was nerfed, and that spec didn't use traditional warrior tier sets anyway. Warrior tank in general got pushed to worst tank spot from first spot. You should never ever wear full T1, T2 or T3 if you want to hold threat against people with purple gear.

I don't have high hopes, but let's hope the 1.18.1 fixes protection warrior itemization and their outdated sets. For now I suggest sticking with T2 shoulders, which are actually pretty good. T2 legs and boots are also strong. The rest of the items are situational at best, and you should use off-pieces like ES helmet instead of T2 helmet or T2 DPS chest instead of T2 tank chest.

I have a suspicion that deep-protection warrior, the spec that is meant to use these items, is the least played tank by a long shot, so developers don't have any data nor receive any criticism or suggestion about them.

subject: Thoughts on Proc Warrior Rework – Identity, Skill Ceiling, and Build Diversity
content_md:
With the upcoming proc warrior talent rework, I wanted to start a thread to share some thoughts and hear the community’s opinions about the current gameplay and the warrior’s identity.

I’ll post my own views here, and I’d really like to see what other people think as well.

First of all, the warrior has always been a high-skill class, and a big part of that identity is stance dancing.
Switching between stances to get the most out of your toolkit is what makes warrior gameplay unique and rewarding.

Because of that, I think Turtle WoW made a great decision by putting Tactical Mastery in the first row of Arms and by adding Defensive Tactics, giving proc warriors more reasons to stance dance.

That said, this also makes warriors harder to play. Right now, warriors need to do a lot more work to get similar results to what other classes (like druids in Bear Form) get just by existing in their form.

For this rework to be successful, I’d really like to see three things:

- “Easy Mode” Talent Build
A way to build proc warriors where you don’t need to stance dance to tank effectively.
This would make the spec more accessible, help bring more warriors into tanking, and keep it balanced with other tank classes.

- “Hard Mode” Stance Dance Build
A build that still rewards active stance dancing, similar to what we have now.
It’s very fun once you get the hang of it, and having a high skill ceiling is a big part of the warrior’s identity.

- A Viable PvP Tank Build
Warrior tanking in PvP is already very fun thanks to its survivability and Shield Slam’s dispel effect, and I’d really like to see this playstyle become more viable and better supported by the new talents.

I also hope more attention is given to the first three rows of the proc warrior talent tree, so PvP players have meaningful choices instead of feeling forced into the same path every time. Piercing Howl is great and pretty much mandatory for PvP, but because of that, everyone ends up taking it. At the same time, talents like Last Stand just don’t feel very impactful in PvP, so they’re rarely a real alternative. It would be nice to have stronger defensive or utility options in those early tiers, so choosing talents feels like a real decision instead of an obligation.

Overall, I hope the rework keeps both accessibility and depth, so new players can enjoy proc warrior while experienced players still have room to master it.

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

While I like the idea, but people will spec "Viable build" anyway regardless of skill.
You can already imagine several easy mode tanking builds, but I doubt they will be used by anyone.

Same for Thunder Clap - you can use it to slow enemies attacks (though it is inferior to Thunderfury effect). But it is available in Defensive stance too.

Regarding first lines - I vote for moving Improved Disarm to 1st row of talents.

I agree and disagree on a few things. To start, I think Defensive Tactics as a deep prot talent was a mistake and arguably bad game design. The idea that a prot warrior needs to leave their tanking stance in order to do their job effectively sounds antithetical and illogical. Unless it's to execute spam a weakened target, it should be a high risk decision to leave defensive stance when tanking. Defensive Tactics would make more sense if they removed the shield requirement and placed it in the fury tree to assist the fury tanking playstyle. But for a deep prot warrior, it doesn't make much sense and doesn't fit the sword and shield tanking style.

But I heavily agree on making prot pvp more viable. Prot has so much pvp potential that could be realized with a little bit of talent support updates in the protection tree. For example, I've always been of the opinion that talents like Improved Disarm need to be in the first or second row of the tree for easier access.
