author: Licata
subject: Master Strike and Precision Cut
content_md:
Master Strike and Arms Execute(by association Precision Cut) feel like running into a brick wall. Seeing the warrior changes for 1.18.1 I thought I'd try to show why I dislike these two talents and give suggestions on how they can be improved.

 **Master Strike:**
 7 impactful effects on a short cooldown and accessible to any spec, sounds amazing. Except at any given time you have the wrong type of weapon for 6 of them, and worse still you don't even have control over which one is available because weapon stats are so important I'll be using the weapon with the highest numbers, not the correct weapon type. There's no guarantee you'll have a weapon of the desired type to switch to that's close or that you'll have the weapon skill items for it, or that a weapon like that exists at all - if I as an arms warrior with a Kruul axe am fighting a boss I want to disarm with Master Strike my closest downgrades are 15 weapon dps down. If I could pick which effect is available on demand before I go into a bossfight that'd be great, but I can't without taking weapons away from others, handicapping my damage or both so I resort to in combat weapon switching.
So to use our swiss army knife talent we have to:
 1 - as you're using your previous ability(as long as it's not casted like slam, which you use a lot with a 2hander) you switch weapons, with a separate keybind and occupying a bag slot just to use one of many Master Strike variants, retriggering the gcd and resetting the swing timer
 2 - use Master Strike, doing pitiful damage
 3 - in the gcd after master strike switch back to your main weapon, resetting the swing timer again
You're doing 3 things, none of which do real damage, not autoattacking for 3-5 seconds depending on dual wield or 2hander for what, a 3 second disarm? The boss actually gets his weapon back and swings it before I do mine. It's easier to go into def stance and use the normal Disarm for an effect that lasts 3 times longer. And that's a debuff that bosses aren't outright immune to. How often do you immobilize and why wouldn't the monster turn and slap you as the only target in melee? Or disorient or silence? 2 second knockdown? Barely lasts longer than master strike's own gcd. Staff parry which is removed if you switch to another weapon? Is this more useful than pulling a shield out?

The problem I see stems from being tied to the mechanics of switching weapons, thematic sure, but incredibly clunky in practice. Trying to stay close to the idea of flexibility above even what other, unspecialized, warriors can do I suggest these:
 **1** - Turn Master Strike into an off-gcd buff to be used in combination with one ability to give it an extra effect. That way you can split the different effects into skills which fit them. My choices would be, starting with the obvious:
 - Hamstring also immobilizes for 4 sec on top of its 15sec slow
 - Shield Block also grants the 10 sec parry buff on top of the single block charge
 - Sunder Armor also disarms for 3 sec on top of applying the armor debuff
 - Thunder Clap knocking down for 2 seconds on top of applying the attack speed slow. I'm hesitant to make it multiple target, but it's a skill that does 100 damage at max rank without any scaling, and gets reduced by armor, and gets resisted, and the knockdown will be almost over by the time you can use your next skill
 - Whirlwind dismounting on hit. I do not hesitate to make this multiple targets because if it was on a single target skill is dismounting a single person really better than immobilizing them? Drop the extra 100% damage when dismounting unless you want warriors to explode packs of mounted people with Sweeping Strikes
 - Silence - I'm not sure. Adding it to Demo Shout fits as being loud enough to disrupt spellcasting around you, and the radius can be additionally specced into to make it even bigger. I'd rather not have it on an interrupt because that defeats the purpose of speccing a second ability that stops spellcasting.

My aim was to attach it to baseline abilities any spec can use on demand without relying on conditional skills like overpower or revenge. Slam would be a fine choice for knockdown as well. If a strict damage option is required to make it attractive for pure dps pumpers in raids add the 100% weapon damage on hit effect to Rend.

 **2** - Assign Master Strike's effects to stances rather than weapon types, they're on a separate gcd from the rest of our abilities so the process of setting up your desired variant and then using master strike flows naturally like the rest of warrior's stance restricted abilities. Since there's 7 effects and disorient as a cc overlaps with some of the others while also ending on damage I'd drop that and pair the rest up like so:
 - battle stance: disarm and silence, shuts down enemy's offense.
 - defensive stance: 10sec parry buff and immobilize, trap an enemy with you to give you parry haste.
 - berserker stance: knockdown and dismount, the risky stance getting the best cc and forcibly dismounting someone fits them not falling on their feet.

 **-------**
 **Precision Cut**
Execute being limited by the target's hp requires it to be worth more than our other skills, second in effectiveness only to the spec's main skill - Mortal Strike, Bloodthirst, Shield Slam.
Under 20% hp Fury stops using filler skills and spends all its surplus rage on Execute instead of dumping with Heroic Strike and using fillers for Windfury. There's a talent deep in Fury that helps that by reducing the base cost so even with the misses inherent to dual wield you can Execute your rage down to 0 and still be able to use it again after 1.5sec of autoattacks.
Prot gets a lot of rage from being hit, but to tank effectively it needs the threat bonus from Def stance. There's a talent deep in Prot which lets you retain that bonus in stances which can use Execute so you can stop using other filler skills and chain Executes instead of Heroic Striking to dump rage.
Arms can't do that. It generates rage once every 3+ seconds so, barring Windfury, it can't Execute more often than that. Even in the Execute phase it is forced to use fillers. So surely there's a talent deep in Arms which solves this, maybe through some sort of refund to let you Execute twice between your white hits. No it just makes it do more damage, except not enough for to be more effective than the filler skill you use all the time - Slam. That's ok, it's still not a dead gcd, you start doing Mortal Strike/Slam + Execute between your swings - you're still Executing in the Execute phase.
Except after you Execute you have 0 rage and if you're unlucky your next swing doesn't crit or proc windfury, rolls low on weapon variance, gets glanced if you lack weaponskill and you end up at 29 rage or less. Not enough to even salvage with 2 Slams. You don't have Enrage, Flurry and Death Wish to boost your rage generation during the Execute phase, you don't have Recklessness on every boss God forbid you're still progressing and use it on a wipe attempt.
The new 1.18.1 Precision Cut will give you more Execute damage bringing the surplus rage to ~26dmg/rage. In my gear Mortal Strike is ~45dmg/rage, Slam is ~70dmg/rage, it's not close. Even the most effective part of Execute - the base damage is lower at 40dmg/rage. With less gear it might compare better, but with less gear you're generating even less rage. Unless you're about to start overcapping your rage or the target is dying right NOW it's better to use Slam, even during the only time Execute is available, even if you've spent 3(please do not make Boundless Anger a prerequisite and make it 6) talent points on it.
Even when I play around it like the 1.18 patch notes mentioned - I'm at high rage from the last white hit, I'm casting a Slam first and Executing second so the next hit gives me rage to keep going - the game still often outplays me by proccing Windfury on the Slam, overcapping my rage and immediately spending it all on an Execute just after my swing reset so I sit there watching the game for 3 seconds before I'm allowed to press buttons again. To pass the time I look at Bloodrage and remember 10 rage doesn't let me Slam or Execute.
It's not only during Execute phase on a boss, it applies to adds as well. The scenario where Execute feels like it did the exact job it was supposed to - quickly dumping lots of rage from a white swing with no cast time to kill an add, freeing the ranged to switch to something that might not die before they finish casting - leaves me with no rage to intercept to the next target. I can't Battle Shout to rebuff, I can't use my increased Demo Shout range to fill downtime as I walk to the target. But say that next target is close and I don't need to intercept - I don't have the rage to Sunder it. I can't interrupt if needed. I can't even REND to maximize the number of ticks. I can only sit and wait for the next autoattack in 3 seconds like a level 14 warrior. Should I, as the Execute class specced into Execute, not Execute adds because it grinds my rotation to a screeching halt?
Whenever Arms Executes it risks ragestarving and you would have to make the scaling rage bonus 150% for a full 100 rage execute to compensate for missing the 1000 damage you could get from one Slam in the next swing. The refund solved this by ensuring we have enough to keep the rotation going in sync with our white swings while in Execute phase. Why was the refund removed and the extra rage scaling now coming back in 1.18.1? A 30% refund without bonus scaling still makes it a DPS gain over Slam when dumping close to full rage, the only time you want to use it even with the scaling bonus anyway, because it doesn't risk being unable to Slam afterward. It wouldn't make Executing twice at 100 rage more effective than Slam + Execute either.

 **1** - Return the 30% refund, lower or remove the extra damage scaling if absolutely needed. Encourages high rage Executes to avoid overcapping without making following low rage Executes effective enough to compete with Mortal Strike/Slam for the refunded rage to prevent chaining. Seems easiest as that's how the talent previously worked. Negatives are Execute gets used less often and possibly hits no harder than it does for other specs.

First Executes are still big due to setting them up with white hits/Mortal Strike/Slam/Sunder/Overpower/Whirlwind for multiple stacks and whatever else. Following Executes are less rewarding to discourage chaining. Negatives are this being a third layer of setting up on top of needing a big rage bar and the target hitting Execute range.
 **3** - Keep the extra Precision Cut scaling, put a cap on the talented Execute for total rage spent that matches the damage of an untalented 100 rage Execute, should be almost 65 total rage with 75% extra scaling. Same Execute damage for less rage, you get rage left to work with afterward, a second Execute is less dmg/rage than Mortal Strike/Slam to discourage chaining. A full Boundless Anger bar lets you max out twice if you want to spend 3 talent points. Negatives are rage cap sounds buggy and Execute doesn't max out higher than other specs, only hits harder when compared to equal rage spent.
 **4** - Keep extra Precision Cut scaling, put a cap of 100 total rage spent on baseline Execute so at the very least we can use Boundless Anger to give ourselves leftover rage without changing anything for other specs. I hate it because you need to wait for 100+ rage to have anything leftover at all, but it's better than dropping to 0 rage with no counterplay.

Precision Cut has to pull double duty - compete for talent points with Enrage and support the Arms Execute phase so it doesn't get completely demolished by Fury stacking Enrage and Death Wish for more rage gen + more Execute damage on top of Flurry haste. When I say "hits no harder" in reality Fury's Executes will hit harder and more often even as 2h Fury because it has cooldowns to use for the Execute phase.

Finally, please do not make Boundless Anger a prerequisite. Right now I can take 3/3 Precision Cut, 2/2 Battlefield Mobility and Piercing Howl, that's perfect. If Boundless Anger is added to the cost of Precision Cut it leaves me with 2 points to spend on Improved Disciplines or Enrage and I've never felt 2 points in either of them are worth it. Dropping utility and wasting points to get to the talent meant to make Arms Execute work is the opposite of fun.

Switching weapons for Master Strike sucks, use stances instead or make it empower specific abilities.
Having 0 rage after Execute feels terrible no matter how hard the actual Execute hit, please let us refund or keep some rage.
I am begging you do not make Boundless Anger a prerequisite to Precision Cut.

7 impactful effects on a short cooldown and accessible to any spec, sounds amazing. Except at any given time you have the wrong type of weapon for 6 of them, and worse still you don't even have control over which one is available because weapon stats are so important I'll be using the weapon with the highest numbers, not the correct weapon type. There's no guarantee you'll have a weapon of the desired type to switch to that's close or that you'll have the weapon skill items for it, or that a weapon like that exists at all - if I as an arms warrior with a Kruul axe am fighting a boss I want to disarm with Master Strike my closest downgrades are 15 weapon dps down. If I could pick which effect is available on demand before I go into a bossfight that'd be great, but I can't without taking weapons away from others, handicapping my damage or both so I resort to in combat weapon switching.
So to use our swiss army knife talent we have to:
1 - as you're using your previous ability(as long as it's not casted like slam, which you use a lot with a 2hander) you switch weapons, with a separate keybind and occupying a bag slot just to use one of many Master Strike variants, retriggering the gcd and resetting the swing timer
2 - use Master Strike, doing pitiful damage
3 - in the gcd after master strike switch back to your main weapon, resetting the swing timer again
You're doing 3 things, none of which do real damage, not autoattacking for 3-5 seconds depending on dual wield or 2hander for what, a 3 second disarm? The boss actually gets his weapon back and swings it before I do mine. It's easier to go into def stance and use the normal Disarm for an effect that lasts 3 times longer. And that's a debuff that bosses aren't outright immune to. How often do you immobilize and why wouldn't the monster turn and slap you as the only target in melee? Or disorient or silence? 2 second knockdown? Barely lasts longer than master strike's own gcd. Staff parry which is removed if you switch to another weapon? Is this more useful than pulling a shield out?

The problem I see stems from being tied to the mechanics of switching weapons, thematic sure, but incredibly clunky in practice. Trying to stay close to the idea of flexibility above even what other, unspecialized, warriors can do I suggest these:
1 - Turn Master Strike into an off-gcd buff to be used in combination with one ability to give it an extra effect. That way you can split the different effects into skills which fit them. My choices would be, starting with the obvious:
- Hamstring also immobilizes for 4 sec on top of its 15sec slow
- Shield Block also grants the 10 sec parry buff on top of the single block charge
- Sunder Armor also disarms for 3 sec on top of applying the armor debuff
- Thunder Clap knocking down for 2 seconds on top of applying the attack speed slow. I'm hesitant to make it multiple target, but it's a skill that does 100 damage at max rank without any scaling, and gets reduced by armor, and gets resisted, and the knockdown will be almost over by the time you can use your next skill
- Whirlwind dismounting on hit. I do not hesitate to make this multiple targets because if it was on a single target skill is dismounting a single person really better than immobilizing them? Drop the extra 100% damage when dismounting unless you want warriors to explode packs of mounted people with Sweeping Strikes
- Silence - I'm not sure. Adding it to Demo Shout fits as being loud enough to disrupt spellcasting around you, and the radius can be additionally specced into to make it even bigger. I'd rather not have it on an interrupt because that defeats the purpose of speccing a second ability that stops spellcasting.

My aim was to attach it to baseline abilities any spec can use on demand without relying on conditional skills like overpower or revenge. Slam would be a fine choice for knockdown as well. If a strict damage option is required to make it attractive for pure dps pumpers in raids add the 100% weapon damage on hit effect to Rend.

2 - Assign Master Strike's effects to stances rather than weapon types, they're on a separate gcd from the rest of our abilities so the process of setting up your desired variant and then using master strike flows naturally like the rest of warrior's stance restricted abilities. Since there's 7 effects and disorient as a cc overlaps with some of the others while also ending on damage I'd drop that and pair the rest up like so:
- battle stance: disarm and silence, shuts down enemy's offense.
- defensive stance: 10sec parry buff and immobilize, trap an enemy with you to give you parry haste.
- berserker stance: knockdown and dismount, the risky stance getting the best cc and forcibly dismounting someone fits them not falling on their feet.

-------

Execute being limited by the target's hp requires it to be worth more than our other skills, second in effectiveness only to the spec's main skill - Mortal Strike, Bloodthirst, Shield Slam.
Under 20% hp Fury stops using filler skills and spends all its surplus rage on Execute instead of dumping with Heroic Strike and using fillers for Windfury. There's a talent deep in Fury that helps that by reducing the base cost so even with the misses inherent to dual wield you can Execute your rage down to 0 and still be able to use it again after 1.5sec of autoattacks.
Prot gets a lot of rage from being hit, but to tank effectively it needs the threat bonus from Def stance. There's a talent deep in Prot which lets you retain that bonus in stances which can use Execute so you can stop using other filler skills and chain Executes instead of Heroic Striking to dump rage.

author: Sylbrosa
subject: Ideas for Warrior in PvP
content_md:
I feel that Arms Warriors are currently falling behind in PvP damage.

I once saw a post describing warriors as a boulder: if you hit correctly, you get the kill; if you miss, you just stand there like a rock, doing nothing. That analogy feels painfully accurate.

Master Strike gave warriors some much-needed versatility, but even with it, the class still feels behind others. Most ranged classes naturally have the upper hand, and we often lack the damage or tools needed to finish off Shamans or Paladins. Rogues are the only class I feel warriors can somewhat handle, thanks to Overpower and Rend — and even then, if I don’t have a trinket to break stuns, I'll just die.

Right now, Arms Warriors feel like sitting ducks in PvP.

It’s supposed to be rock-paper-scissors, but it feels more like rock-paper-scissors where you can only lose.  crying_turtle

So I’d like to suggest ways to bring better balance. If we follow the rock-paper-scissors idea, warriors should have an advantage against melee and physical-damage classes, while being slightly disadvantaged against casters.

Let’s group the classes like this:

 **Fighters**: Warriors, Paladins
 **Mid-range**: Rogues, Hunters, Feral (Cat) Druids, 2H Shamans
 **Casters**: Priests, Balance Druids, Mages, Warlocks, Elemental Shamans

And the intended matchup flow would be:

Fighters beat mid-range
Mid-range beats casters
Casters beat fighters

I’m intentionally not including healers in this breakdown. While healers are absolutely crucial in group PvP, my goal here is to discuss class-to-class balance and individual matchups.

I also know there will be comments saying, *“But warriors have Mortal Strike, you need to factor that in because it’s huge against healers.”* And I agree — Mortal Strike is extremely important in healer interactions. But that’s a separate discussion about PvP objectives and healer balance, not about how different DPS classes perform against each other in direct combat.

And yes, I also expect the classic *“warriors are great if you have a pocket healer or two”* argument. But let’s be honest: every class performs better with dedicated healing support. That’s not unique to warriors, and it doesn’t really address how the class feels or performs in standard PvP encounters or smaller skirmishes.

Here are some ideas to improve the Arms Warrior PvP experience by giving the class better tools against Rogues, Hunters, and 2H Shamans — without breaking class identity or making warriors overpowered.

 **1. New Ability — Nachreisen**

Effect: Becomes available after **the Warrior's attack get's parried**. Deals weapon damage %.

Casters won’t be parrying warrior attacks, so this ability would mainly affect matchups against fighters and mid-range classes. It would give warriors extra pressure where they are supposed to be strong, without impacting PvE damage.

It also keeps the warrior’s high skill-cap identity: the player must recognize when the ability is available and against which targets it’s effective, making it a reactive, skill-based tool.

 **2. Victory Rush / Momentum After a Kill**

The warrior is a boulder: once it gets rolling, it should keep rolling.

If free damage from Victory Rush is not desirable, the same idea could be implemented in other ways — for example, resetting Intercept on kill, allowing the warrior to quickly move to the next target.

This still keeps warriors disadvantaged against casters, since Intercept would not be available to deal with Blink, roots, or crowd control unless a kill has already happened. It would play similarly to how Charge works at the start of an engagement. If you want to make sure the warrior is directly responsible for the kill. Bake it into Execute.

 **3. Improved Deflection for Two-Handed Arms**

Add a skill-based parry mechanic for two-handed weapons, similar to Shield Block, deep in the Arms tree — possibly even combined with Sweeping Strikes.

Ideally, it would have its own cooldown separate from the global cooldown, making it more skill-based and reactive. This would improve survivability against fighters and mid-range classes, without affecting matchups against casters.

 **Notice that abilities #1 and #3 don't interact.**

I believe these three changes would greatly improve the Arms Warrior PvP experience without making the class overpowered.

Most importantly, abilities #1 and #3 would give developers tuning knobs that affect only PvP matchups against fighters and mid-range classes, without impacting PvE balance. By adjusting these tools, they could fine-tune warrior performance where it matters, instead of globally buffing damage.

And since they **don't interact** you can fine-tune DPS or survivability separately. Although if these are implemented. You can expect players to complain about them not interacting and saying they should. Because everyone wants a powerspike  hiding_smth_turtle_head

I’d love to hear other ideas as well. **Please comment and upvote**  so the developers can see these suggestions and the discussion around them.

author: Ellifta
subject: Simple Fixes for Protection Warrior
content_md:
It's common knowledge by now that warrior tank is severely lacking compared to other tanks in threat department. Arguably also in mitigation department, since taking the defensive tactics talents to do more threat requires leaving defensive stance and foregoing 10%DR that comes with it.

The forum is full of many protection warrior suggestions, but I think they reinvent the wheel by revamping the protection tree or making grandiose changes that don't fit much with the vanilla+ . Therefore, I wanted to offer my thoughts on very simple fixes that developers could literally implement overnight with the experience I have from having played warrior with tanking only for 155 days and 13 hours.

 1 - Add Scaling to Revenge
Currently a lot of warrior abilities like sunder armor and revenge have fixed threat values that don't scale with any of your stats. This means there is no difference in threat done between a fresh 60 and Kara40 geared warrior. The solution is quite simple: Add 20% AP scaling to revenge. A Kara40 geared warrior tank will have between 1500-2100 AP depending on their gear and raid group. This would turn the ability into a decent filler whenever it pops since it would now deal quite a bit of damage against bosses once they get 5x sunder + FF + CoR. In PvP this would change absolutely nothing, since revenge is physical damage and is reduced by armor. Revenge should also be available in battle stance if the talent "Defensive Tactics" is taken.

 2 - Some Number Tweaks
A lot of people don't know that warriors have an inherent 0.8 multiplier to their threat in battle stance and berserker stance. This is why, despite the massive 180% threat multiplier listed on "Defensive Tactics" talent, the actual threat ends up being almost the same. To fix this, the developers can simply increase the threat multiplier granted by "Defiance" and "Defensive Tactics" even higher. As of the time of this post, next patch will increase Defiance from 15% to 20%, but I think 25% is even a better number. Additionally, the 180% threat multiplier from Defensive Tactics should be increased to 250%.

 3 - Minor Talent Tweaks
The deep protection talent "One Handed Specialization" should reduce the chance of being parried/blocked/dodged by 1% for each point, up to 5% reduction on boss avoidance. A lot of people don't know that bosses have a 14% chance to parry attacks from front, then a 5% chance to dodge on top of that. This would minimize the chances of getting screwed over by RNG at the start of boss fights where you get "parry, parry, block". It's also deep enough in protection tree that only deep protection tanks can take it.

Shield block charges gained from shield slam and shield block should stack. You should not have to play piano and watch whether boss managed to hit you or not to be crush immune in defensive stance. Currently, they cancel each other out. It's incredibly stupid and pointless. I know the point was to prevent Fury prot from being crit-crush immune, but if you have the shield slam talent, you are already not fury-prot, so there's no need for these bonuses to not stack.

And that's it. That's all that would take to make warrior a great tank again. Warrior doesn't have to be good at AoE, have the best threat or mitigation amongst tanks, but it should be the most reliable single target tank. The warrior tank already foregoes 10% DR by switching to battle stance if using the talent "Defensive Tactics". It also lacks AoE the paladin tanks have. It just makes sense that they should have the second best single target TPS after a bear.

Protection tank in battle stance should be just under a bear tank in terms of threat and above the rest. Protection tank in defensive stance should be on-par or slightly worse than a paladin in single target threat.

author: Morkahja
subject: Re: Simple Fixes for Protection Warrior
content_md:
First of all, Turtle WoW isn’t Vanilla+. Yes, it’s the closest thing we have to Vanilla+, but as I remember reading, it is *“a fan-made expansion story for Vanilla World of Warcraft that delves deeper into exploring the original lore of the game”* (literally the first sentence on the website).
So please don’t react to ideas with the mindset of this being Vanilla+. Allow it to be its own ****EXPANSION****, and with that, allow space for changes that are actually bold.

Your improvements aren’t bad, in my opinion, even if they mostly just tweak things a little.

 1. It doesn’t really matter that much, but yes, I think in general all abilities should scale in some way.
 2. Yes, more threat is always nice; that’s pretty much what we’re being promised in the next patch anyway.
 3. Check out the talent in my custom talent tree for Prot Warrior (my little dream), which directly addresses the issue with Shield Slam by changing Improved Shield Slam:
[[https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... Z89v8fans4](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t2=Z89v8fans4)]([https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... Z89v8fans4](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t2=Z89v8fans4))

I don’t really understand why you think a deep Prot warrior should be worse than a paladin in single-target threat. I strongly disagree. In my opinion, deep Prot should have roughly the same single-target threat as a druid tank, since both are primarily single-target tanks, while paladins and shamans should excel at group threat.

I also question whether we should always continue giving Fury/Prot more threat. Maybe it’s enough that Fury/Prot does more damage, but has the same or even less single-target threat, or shifts its strength toward group threat and add control instead of pure boss threat. That could be a way to give warriors the tools to act as a kind of Fury/Prot AoE tank, while deep Prot clearly excels as the single-target tank.

Since warriors effectively have two tank specs—unlike other classes—this could be a strong new identity: three distinct roles within one class framework—DPS, AoE tank, and single-target tank.

Just my humble opinion.

Barring that, prot warrior specifically needs its tps generation diversified out of shield slam so that they're not sitting useless for 4.5s at a time if a shield slam gets dodge/parried.

So, for my understanding: is your argument for wanting an ability or attack that is unavoidable (but still can Miss) is so a Sword+Board Warrior does not lose Threat in the seconds between multiple avoidance mechanics from a raid boss?

According to the patchnotes, In the next patch (1.18.1), Bears will be getting their Threat reduced on certain abilities. Warriors will be getting a 5% increase in Threat through a rework of the talent 'Defiance'.

What I do understand though (when only concentrating on single target tanking) is that Warriors have abilities aligned with the Bear (and some more) that also generate Threat in the same manner:

 1. Bear 'Swipe' - has no cd save the gcd. Warrior has Sunder Armor which also has no cd save the gcd.

 2. Bear 'Maul' - on next swing, uses flat damage, and has an inflexible swing timer of 2.5s. Warrior has HS on next swing that does weapon damage + flat damage, and has a flexible swing timer (based off your mainhand weapon speed)

 3. Bear 'Savage Bite' - excellent ability, works off weapon damage + flat damage, and as you say off the gcd. Has a 6 second cd. The closest ability a Warrior has to that would be Shield Slam (similar cd, when untalented), damage modified by AP + flat damage, but does suffer the gcd.

However, as for your statement regarding the Bear being able to deliver 3 hits on any given target, this would only be possible with an abundance of Rage, as the last patch (1.18) stopped 'on swing' abilities being queued without having the Rage required to perform the ability. As a Warrior, having an abundance of Rage coupled with a fast weapon allows spamming HS.

Warrior also has 'Concussion Blow' which costs no Rage, gives Rage, and cannot be resisted by armour (has a long cd though).
Furthermore, a deep prot / Concussion Blow Warrior is likely to pick up the 'Defensive Tactics' talent making tanking in Arms & Berserker stance viable, and by that extention further increasing Threat through damage by not being in Defensive Stance and therefore, not suffering the attack damage penalty (10%).

I feel all this just makes Warrior tanking more fun by being more flexible, and more challenging, further adding to the fun.

....it can also be quite stressful too, but you can't paint a picture without both light & dark! :)

subject: Simple Change, Big performance

Please consider adding a new talent called Guardian's Revenge in the same row as Defensive Tactics.

What does it do? It improves Revenge by fulfilling the Reprisal requirement: Revenge is now also activated when an ally is hit by a direct melee attack from a creature (AKA: your friend has the threat). AoE attacks and cleaves do not count. It also grants additional bonus threat to Revenge.

author: Wilsonsds
subject: Re: Simple Change, Big performance
content_md:
I do not think “there is no existing example” is enough to call it impossible. This would not be a simple database-only talent, but I believe it is scriptable on the server side.

As far as I know, the server can already react to combat proc events, identify who was hit, who attacked, and restrict effects to a specific valid target. Revenge itself is already a reactive ability based on combat events, so this would be more of an extension of its trigger conditions rather than a completely new mechanic.

The real question is whether the developers consider the scripting effort and edge-case filtering worthwhile. However, this kind of script could also open doors for other similar mechanics in the future.

author: SvenS2
subject: Re: Simple Change, Big performance
content_md:
> **Xudo wrote: Wed Mar 11, 2026 6:20 am**
> I don't think it is possible. Do you have any examples of this in other spells?

It's possible to implement in Warcraft 3's engine via just GUI commands, so it should be possible in WoW's. A very oversimplified example:

1. Event handler for on attack event.
2. Pick all units within X radius of the player character, where picked unit is of type ally && in party.
3. If Attack on picked unit is Melee && picked unit =/= player character.
4. Then change Revenge's active flag on.
5. Apply talent CD or have it by proc based.

As for example for similar abilities in WoW, talents that check for Critical Hits by allies works on a similar principle

The only part that I'm not sure is feasible is the ability being enabled only vs the unit that issued the attack. Might be pretty wonky, plus I don't see a reason to place such a restriction, so long as the talent is proc or CD based.

author: SvenS2
subject: Move "Unbridled Wrath" to the Protection tree
content_md:
Hey there, I've been thinking how to improve the protection leveling experience, without introducing more damage and without affecting late game too much, and the following idea came up.

Replace ****Iron Will**** in the Protection tree with ****Unbridled Wrath**** and apply the following changes:

 1. Update the name so it fits the protection tree better. "Focused Rage" maybe?
 2. Update the effect to: "Gives you a 15/30/45/60/75% chance to generate an additional Rage point when you deal melee damage with a weapon. The effect is doubled for two-handed weapons****or while using a shield**.**"
---
 **Pros:**
1. Warriors using a shield will have better rage generation during the early stages of the game.
2. Rage through Unbridled Wrath is counted as power gain, so it causes a small amount of threat (minor but flavorful addition to the tank oriented spec).
 **Cons:**
1. "Unbridled Wrath" is currently the talent choice for 2h Fury warriors. This means they'll either have to take Booming Voice or the substitute talent must accommodate that playstyle.
 ****Thoughts and neutral points:****
1. Moving "Unbridled Wrath" to the protection tree won't affect Fury-Prot.
2. For leveling, duel-wielding warriors skip on "Unbridled Wrath", because  "Duel Wield Specialization" provides significantly more rage due to more successful and harder hitting offhand hits. And the talents from row 3 and onwards are too good to skip out on.
3. Currently, during the early-mid game, Shield Specialization does not generate enough rage to make it on par with Duel Wielding or 2H Warriors.
4. Tanking in classic and especially in Turtle WoW as a warrior is extremely easy. You don't need to invest a single point into the prot tree until late game, and a lot of encounters can be handled without even using a shield. So why bother improving Prot then? Well, a lot of players like custom challenges, roleplay or just enjoy the shield focused playstyle. So the aim is to improve the leveling process for them
 **Concerns and open topics:**
1. What do we do with "Iron Will"? Should it be placed on Row 2 of Fury, in place of "Unbridled Wrath", or should it be merged with another Prot talent?
2. If "Iron Will" gets merged with another prot talent or outright removed, then what should the "Unbridled Wrath" substitute in the Fury tree be? Imo it should still be something that favors 2h warriors.
